   315	\begin{proof}
   316		\uses{def:v-swap-unitary, lem:v-swap-conjugation, lem:tildew-product-form, lem:qld-construct-the-paulis, lem:qld-win-implications, fact:triangle-for-simeq, def:bracket, lem:cancellation, lem:schwartz-zippel-total-degree, lem:qld-4-7}
   317		For the first item, the self-consistency of the observables $\tilde{W}^j$ (Item~2 of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-construct-the-paulis}) is equivalent, since these observables are Hermitian involutions (Lemma~\ref{lem:tildew-product-form}), to $\E_{j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}} \E_{\tilde{u} \in \F_q^M} \bra{\hat\psi} \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \ot \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \ket{\hat\psi} \geq 1 - \delta_P/2$; setting $\ket{\vartheta} = V_{\mathrm{A}} \ot V_{\mathrm{B}} \ket{\hat\psi}$ and using the exact conjugation identities of Lemma~\ref{lem:v-swap-conjugation}, this becomes $\bra{\vartheta} H_W \ket{\vartheta} \geq 1 - \delta_P/2$ for $W \in \{X,Z\}$, where $H_W = \E_j \E_{\tilde{u}} \, \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \ot \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) = \bigl( \E_{s \in \F_q} \tau^W(s) \ot \tau^W(s) \bigr)^{\ot M}$ by the tensor factorization of $\tau^W(\tilde{u})$ and the invariance of the uniform average over $s$ under $s \mapsto e_j s$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:cancellation}, $\E_{s,s'} \tau^X(s)\tau^Z(s') \ot \tau^X(s)\tau^Z(s') = \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}\bra{\mathrm{EPR}_q}$ on each pair of qudits, whence $H_X H_Z = \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}\bra{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}$. The bounds $\| (\Id - H_W)\ket{\vartheta} \|^2 \leq \delta_P$ and $\bra{\vartheta} H_W^2 \ket{\vartheta} \geq 1 - 2\delta_P$, combined through the triangle inequality $\| H_X \ket{\vartheta} - H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \| \leq 2\sqrt{\delta_P}$ (see Remark~\ref{rem:qld-unitary-triangle-slip}), give $\bra{\vartheta} \Id_{\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'} \ot (\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}\bra{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M})_{\mathrm{A}''\mathrm{B}''} \ket{\vartheta} \geq 1 - 4\delta_P$.
   318		% Case distinction added: the source normalizes the projected vector
   319		% without ensuring that it is nonzero; see Remark rem:qld-unitary-triangle-slip.
   320		If $\delta_P > 1/8$, then, after enlarging the universal constant in $\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}$, both items of the lemma hold with $\ket{\mathrm{aux}}$ an arbitrary unit state, since their left-hand sides never exceed $4$; assume therefore $\delta_P \leq 1/8$. Then the vector $(\bra{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M})_{\mathrm{A}''\mathrm{B}''} \ket{\vartheta}$ has squared norm at least $1 - 4\delta_P \geq 1/2 > 0$, and $\ket{\mathrm{aux}}$ may be defined as its normalization; the overlap of $\ket{\vartheta}$ with $\ket{\mathrm{aux}} \ot \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}$ equals the norm of that vector and is at least $\sqrt{1 - 4\delta_P} \geq 1 - 4\delta_P$, which yields the first item with a bound of $8\delta_P = O(\sqrt{\delta_P})$. For the second item, Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-win-implications} gives, on average over $u \in \F_q^m$, $M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \ot \Id \simeq_\eps \Id \ot M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a$ and $\Id \ot M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a \simeq_\eps M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a \ot \Id$, where $M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} = \sum_{h : g_h(u) = a} M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h$; combining these with Item~1 of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-construct-the-paulis} by Lemma~\ref{fact:triangle-for-simeq}, using $\eps \leq \sqrt{\eps} \leq \delta_P$, yields $M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \ot \Id \simeq_{\sqrt{\delta_P}} \Id \ot \tilde{M}^{W,\mathrm{ind}_m(u)}_a$. Writing $\ket{\Delta} = \ket{\mathrm{aux}} \ot \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}$, the quantity to be bounded for the $\mathrm{A}$-side relation equals $2 - 2\sum_h \bra{\Delta} V_{\mathrm{A}} M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h V_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger \ot (\tau^W_h)_{\mathrm{B}''} \ket{\Delta}$, since $(\tau^W_h)_{\mathrm{A}''} \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M} = (\tau^W_h)_{\mathrm{B}''} \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}$. Replacing $(\tau^W_h)_{\mathrm{B}''}$ by the averaged coarse-graining $\E_u \sum_{h' : g_{h'}(u) = g_h(u)} (\tau^W_{h'})_{\mathrm{B}''}$ costs at most $md/q$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:schwartz-zippel-total-degree} (distinct $h \neq h'$ have distinct encodings $g_h \neq g_{h'}$, of total degree at most $md$), and by \eqref{eq:qld-unitary-6} the resulting sum equals $\E_u \sum_{a} \bra{\Delta} V_{\mathrm{A}} M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} V_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger \ot V_{\mathrm{B}} \tilde{M}^{W,\mathrm{ind}_m(u)}_a V_{\mathrm{B}}^\dagger \ket{\Delta}$. Exchanging $\ket{\Delta}$ for $\ket{\vartheta}$ costs $O(\delta_P^{1/4})$ by the first item, and the resulting expression $\E_u \sum_a \bra{\hat\psi} M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \ot \tilde{M}^{W,\mathrm{ind}_m(u)}_a \ket{\hat\psi}$ is at least $1 - O(\sqrt{\delta_P})$ by the $\simeq_{\sqrt{\delta_P}}$ relation above. Altogether the distance is $O(\delta_P^{1/4} + md/q)$; the $\mathrm{B}$-side relation is proved identically.
   321	\end{proof}

   323	\begin{remark}[Two steps in the source proof of the extraction lemma]\label{rem:qld-unitary-triangle-slip}
   324		In the source proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-unitary}, the triangle inequality gives $\| H_X \ket{\vartheta} - H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \| \leq \| (\Id - H_X)\ket{\vartheta} \| + \| (\Id - H_Z)\ket{\vartheta} \| \leq 2\sqrt{\delta_P}$, so that $\| H_X \ket{\vartheta} - H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \|^2 \leq 4\delta_P$; the source instead asserts the bound $2\sqrt{\delta_P}$ for the \emph{squared} norm, which holds only when $\sqrt{\delta_P} \leq 1/2$, and consequently carries the term $\sqrt{\delta_P}$ into an overlap bound of $1 - 2\delta_P - \sqrt{\delta_P}$. The proof above uses the corrected bound $4\delta_P$, which gives the overlap bound $1 - 4\delta_P$ and leaves the final bound $\delta_{\mathrm{qld}} = O(\delta_P^{1/4} + md/q)$ unchanged. The source proof also normalizes the vector $(\bra{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M})_{\mathrm{A}''\mathrm{B}''} \ket{\vartheta}$ without ensuring that it is nonzero; the case distinction on $\delta_P$ in the proof above supplies this, the conclusions of the lemma being trivial when $\delta_P$ exceeds a universal constant.
   325	\end{remark}

   327	\section{Proof of the soundness of the Pauli basis test}
   328	
   329	We can now prove the soundness theorem for the Pauli basis test, stated as Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli} in Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-test}.
   330	
   331	\begin{proof}
   332		\proves{thm:pauli}
   333		\uses{lem:qld-unitary, lem:pauli-completeness, thm:naimark, lem:projective-strategy-setup, def:expanded-state, def:EPR, def:povm-distance}
   334		Let $(\ket{\psi},M)$ be a strategy for $\mathfrak{G}^{\mathrm{Pauli}}_{(q,m,d)}$ that succeeds with probability at least $1 - \eps$, where $\ket{\psi}$ is a bipartite state on registers $\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathrm{B}$. By Naimark's theorem (Theorem~\ref{thm:naimark}, as formulated in~\cite[Theorem 5.1]{Ji2020LowIndividualDegree}), at the cost of extending $\ket{\psi}$ by sufficiently many ancilla qubits initialized in the state $\ket{0}$, we may assume that the strategy is projective and that the state is padded as in the conventions of Lemma~\ref{lem:projective-strategy-setup} and the convention following it. Let $V_{\mathrm{A}}$ be the unitary acting on registers $\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''$ given by Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-unitary}, and let $\phi_{\mathrm{A}}$ be the isometry mapping register $\mathrm{A}$ to registers $\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''$, where $\mathrm{A}'$ and $\mathrm{A}''$ are isomorphic to $(\C^q)^{\ot M}$, defined by
   335		\[
   336			\phi_{\mathrm{A}}\colon \ket{\theta}_{\mathrm{A}} \mapsto V_{\mathrm{A}} \bigl(\ket{\theta}_{\mathrm{A}} \ot (\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M})_{\mathrm{A}' \mathrm{A}''}\bigr)\;;
   337		\]
   338		define $\phi_{\mathrm{B}}$ analogously.
   339		% Reliance disclosure added: the proof chain of thm:pauli passes through
   340		% lem:qld-4-7, whose source proof (lines 1277--1413 of
   341		% 14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex) instantiates the classical low
   342		% individual degree test at dimension 2m+2 without a divisibility
   343		% hypothesis; the sentence below records the resulting outstanding
   344		% obligation.
   345		This invocation is where the analysis of the classical low individual degree test enters: Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-unitary} rests on the polynomial-pair measurement of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-7}, whose proof instantiates the classical test in $2m+2$ variables and at present does so only when $2m+2$ divides $q$ --- a divisibility that fails for every admissible tuple with $m \geq 2$. Three further steps of that same chain are likewise unproved. The classical soundness statement invoked there, Theorem~\ref{lem:ld-soundness}, is imported from Theorem~4.7 of~\cite{Ji2021Quantum} through an identification of the game $\mathfrak{G}^{\mathrm{ld}}_{(q,m,d,1)}$ with the two-prover tensor-code test for $\code^{\ot m}$, and neither that game correspondence nor the bound on the auxiliary parameter of Theorem~4.7 under which the stated error function $\delta_{\mathrm{ld}}$ is obtained has been established; both, with the divisibility obstruction, are documented in \cite{gap:qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility}. Furthermore, the combined-lines consistency of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-13}, which Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-7} consumes, is established here only with the error $m \cdot \poly(\eps, md/q)$, the error form $\poly(m^2 \eps, md/q)$ carried in its statement remaining unproved (see \cite{gap:qpbt_combined-lines-error-term}). The present proof is therefore complete only modulo these four obligations. Since the expanded state $\ket{\hat\psi}$ of Definition~\ref{def:expanded-state} is exactly $\ket{\psi}$ with the halves of $M$ pairs $\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}$ appended locally in registers $\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''$ and $\mathrm{B}'\mathrm{B}''$, we have $\phi_{\mathrm{A}} \ot \phi_{\mathrm{B}} \ket{\psi} = V_{\mathrm{A}} \ot V_{\mathrm{B}} \ket{\hat\psi}$. Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-unitary} therefore yields a state $\ket{\mathrm{aux}}$ on registers $\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'$ such that
   346		\[
   347			\bigl\| \phi_{\mathrm{A}} \ot \phi_{\mathrm{B}} \ket{\psi} - \ket{\mathrm{aux}} \ot \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M} \bigr\|^2 \leq \delta_{\mathrm{qld}}\;.
   348		\]
   349		% Transfer step added: the source (lines 1864--1875 of
   350		% 14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex) passes directly from the
   351		% conjugation estimates of lem:qld-unitary, which concern the
   352		% unitarily conjugated operators V (M_h ot Id) V^dagger, to the
   353		% corresponding estimates for the isometry phi, whose conjugation
   354		% inserts the projection onto its range; the range-projection
   355		% argument below supplies the missing step.
   356		Item~2 of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-unitary} concerns the unitarily conjugated operators $N^W_h = V_{\mathrm{A}} \, (M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h)_{\mathrm{A}} \, V_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger$, whereas conjugation by the isometry $\phi_{\mathrm{A}}$ additionally inserts the projection $Q_{\mathrm{A}} = \phi_{\mathrm{A}} \phi_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger = V_{\mathrm{A}} \, \bigl(\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}\bra{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}\bigr)_{\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''} \, V_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger$ onto the range of $\phi_{\mathrm{A}}$: since $(M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h)_{\mathrm{A}}$ and $\bigl(\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}\bra{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}\bigr)_{\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''}$ act on disjoint registers and hence commute,
   357		\[
   358			\phi_{\mathrm{A}} \, (M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h)_{\mathrm{A}} \, \phi_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger
   359			= V_{\mathrm{A}} \, \Bigl( (M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h)_{\mathrm{A}} \ot \bigl(\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}\bra{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}\bigr)_{\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''} \Bigr) \, V_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger
   360			= N^W_h \, Q_{\mathrm{A}} = Q_{\mathrm{A}} \, N^W_h\;.
   361		\]
   362		The estimates transfer from $N^W_h$ to $\phi_{\mathrm{A}} \, (M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h)_{\mathrm{A}} \, \phi_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger$ as follows. Write $\ket{\Delta} = \ket{\mathrm{aux}} \ot \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}$ and $\ket{\vartheta} = \phi_{\mathrm{A}} \ot \phi_{\mathrm{B}} \ket{\psi}$. Since $\phi_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger \phi_{\mathrm{A}} = \Id$, the projection $\Id - Q_{\mathrm{A}}$ annihilates $\ket{\vartheta}$, so the displayed bound above gives
   363		\[
   364			\bigl\| (\Id - Q_{\mathrm{A}}) \ket{\Delta} \bigr\|^2
   365			= \bigl\| (\Id - Q_{\mathrm{A}}) (\ket{\Delta} - \ket{\vartheta}) \bigr\|^2
   366			\leq \bigl\| \ket{\Delta} - \ket{\vartheta} \bigr\|^2
   367			\leq \delta_{\mathrm{qld}}\;.
   368		\]
   369		Since the strategy is projective, the operators $N^W_h$, for $h \in \F_q^M$, are mutually orthogonal projectors summing to the identity, so $\sum_h \| N^W_h \ket{\xi} \|^2 = \| \ket{\xi} \|^2$ for every vector $\ket{\xi}$. Decomposing
   370		\[
   371			\bigl( \phi_{\mathrm{A}} \, (M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h)_{\mathrm{A}} \, \phi_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger - (\tau^W_h)_{\mathrm{A}''} \bigr) \ket{\Delta}
   372			= \bigl( N^W_h - (\tau^W_h)_{\mathrm{A}''} \bigr) \ket{\Delta} - N^W_h (\Id - Q_{\mathrm{A}}) \ket{\Delta}
   373		\]
   374		and summing the squared norms over $h$ via $\| \xi - \xi' \|^2 \leq 2\|\xi\|^2 + 2\|\xi'\|^2$, the first terms contribute $O(\delta_{\mathrm{qld}})$ by Item~2 of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-unitary} and the second terms contribute at most $2 \| (\Id - Q_{\mathrm{A}}) \ket{\Delta} \|^2 \leq 2\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}$; hence, for $W \in \{X,Z\}$,
   375		\[
   376			\phi_{\mathrm{A}} \, (M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h)_{\mathrm{A}} \, \phi_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger \approx_{\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}} (\tau^W_h)_{\mathrm{A}''}
   377			\qquad \text{and, by the identical argument,} \qquad
   378			\phi_{\mathrm{B}} \, (M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h)_{\mathrm{B}} \, \phi_{\mathrm{B}}^\dagger \approx_{\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}} (\tau^W_h)_{\mathrm{B}''}\;,
   379		\]
   380		where the $\approx$ statements hold with respect to the state $\ket{\mathrm{aux}} \ot \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}$ and the answer summation is over $h \in \F_q^M$; the constant implicit in $\approx_{\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}}$ (Definition~\ref{def:povm-distance}) absorbs the factors accumulated above. This shows that the game $\mathfrak{G}^{\mathrm{Pauli}}_{(q,m,d)}$ is a self-test, with robustness $\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}(\eps,m,d,q)$, for the canonical Pauli strategy of Lemma~\ref{lem:pauli-completeness}. Identifying the registers $\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'$ with $\mathrm{A}'$ and $\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'$ with $\mathrm{B}'$ matches the statement of Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli}, in which $\phi_{\mathrm{A}}\colon \mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{A}} \to \mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{A}'} \ot \mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{A}''}$. Finally, unpacking the dependence on the parameters $\eps, m, d, q$, the function $\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}(\eps,m,d,q) = O(\delta_P^{1/4} + md/q)$ has the form $a(md)^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$ for universal constants $a > 1$ and $0 < b < 1$; here $\delta_P = C(\delta_G + \sqrt{\eps} + md/q)$ and $\delta_G$ already has that form. See Remark~\ref{rem:pauli-robustness-form} for the reconciliation with the statement of Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli}.
   381	\end{proof}
   382	
   383	\begin{remark}[Norm conventions in the robustness bound]\label{rem:pauli-robustness-form}
   384		The proof above, following the source, establishes the first conclusion of Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli} in the squared form $\| \phi_{\mathrm{A}} \ot \phi_{\mathrm{B}} \ket{\psi} - \ket{\mathrm{aux}} \ot \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M} \|^2 \leq \delta_{\mathrm{qld}}$, whereas the theorem bounds the unsquared norm by $\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}(\eps,m,d,q)$. The two are reconciled by replacing the exponent $b$ with $b/2$ and enlarging $a$, since the class of functions $a(md)^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$ is closed under square roots up to such adjustments of the universal constants. Similarly, the closing sentence of the source proof asserts constants $a > 1$ and $0 < b < 1$, while Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli} requires only $a \geq 1$ and $0 < b < 1$; the former implies the latter.
   385	\end{remark}

    34	\section{Key theorem forms}
    35	
    36	Let $e_1,\ldots,e_t$ be the fixed self-dual basis of $\mathbb F_q$ over
    37	$\mathbb F_2$.  With the phase convention of the source, generalized Pauli
    38	observables satisfy
    39	\[
    40	  \tau^X(a)\tau^Z(b)
    41	  =(-1)^{\operatorname{tr}(a\mathbin{\cdot}b)}
    42	   \tau^Z(b)\tau^X(a).
    43	\]
    44	Substituting $a=e_j\widetilde u$ and $b=e_{j'}\widetilde v$ gives the exact
    45	relation
    46	\[
    47	  \widetilde X^j(\widetilde u)\widetilde Z^{j'}(\widetilde v)
    48	  =(-1)^{\operatorname{tr}
    49	      (e_je_{j'}(\widetilde u\mathbin{\cdot}\widetilde v))}
    50	   \widetilde Z^{j'}(\widetilde v)\widetilde X^j(\widetilde u).
    51	\]
    52	This formula applies uniformly, whether or not $j=j'$.
    53	
    54	\section{The false dichotomy in the source}
    55	
    56	Lines~1438--1450 of
    57	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex}
    58	identify each extracted observable with a tensor product containing
    59	$\tau^W(e_j\widetilde u)$.  Lines~1451--1456 then claim that the extracted
    60	$X$- and $Z$-observables commute whenever $j\neq j'$
    61	\cite[lines~1438--1456]{Ji2020MIPStar}.  Self-duality gives only
    62	\[
    63	  \operatorname{tr}(e_je_{j'})=0 \qquad (j\neq j').
    64	\]
    65	It does not imply
    66	\[
    67	  \operatorname{tr}(e_je_{j'}s)=0
    68	  \qquad\text{for every }s\in\mathbb F_q.
    69	\]

    72	pairing is nondegenerate, so there is an $s\in\mathbb F_q$ for which
    73	$\operatorname{tr}(cs)=1$.  Taking vectors whose first coordinates are $1$
    74	and $s$, with all remaining coordinates zero, gives

   103	local correction rather than an additional hypothesis on the extraction

    51	More generally, the second identity holds for a polynomial outcome $g$ under
    52	the explicit hypothesis that $g$ belongs to the image of the encoding; no
    53	converse is asserted.

    55	For an arbitrary bounded individual-degree polynomial $g$, the Boolean values
    56	determine its multilinear interpolant, not necessarily $g$ itself.  The
    57	unrestricted identity

    37	
    38	\section{Key theorem forms}
    39	
    40	Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, let $\rho$ be an arbitrary
    41	density operator on $H$, and let $u\mapsto O^u$ be binary observables on $H$,
    42	indexed by $\mathbb F_2^t$.  The cited theorem assumes the averaged
    43	correlation estimate
    44	\[
    45	  \mathop{\mathbb E}_{u,v}
    46	  \operatorname{Tr}\!\left(O^u O^v O^{u+v}\rho\right) \geq 1-\delta.
    47	\]
    48	It produces an auxiliary space $H'$, a unit vector $\mathrm{anc}\in H'$, and
    49	binary observables $L^u$ on $H\otimes H'$ satisfying, with
    50	$\rho'=\rho\otimes|\mathrm{anc}\rangle\langle\mathrm{anc}|$,
    51	\[
    52	  L^uL^v=L^{u+v}
    53	  \quad\text{for every }u,v.
    54	\]
    55	Moreover,
    56	\[
    57	  \mathop{\mathbb E}_{u}
    58	  \operatorname{Tr}\!\left((L^u-O^u\otimes I_{H'})^\dagger
    59	    (L^u-O^u\otimes I_{H'})\,\rho'\right)\leq\delta.
    60	\]
    61	In particular, $L^0=I$: exact linearity gives $(L^0)^2=L^0$, while an
    62	observable is invertible.
    63	
    64	The chapter needs a parameterized version.  For each pair $(x,z)$ it applies
    65	the theorem to $(r,s)\mapsto O^{x,z,r,s}$.  Since the provider theorem accepts
    66	the actual nonnegative defect on each fiber, no assumption that a fiber defect
    67	is at most one, and no good--bad fiber split, is needed.  One must still
    68	formulate the finite common-extension step that makes the auxiliary space
    69	uniform over $(x,z)$.

    71	\section{Comparison with the quoted statement}
    72	
    73	Lines~711--725 of
    74	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex} quote the
    75	linearity theorem.  The displayed hypothesis correctly averages over both
    76	group variables.  The displayed conclusion, however, says that the corrected
    77	observable is close for every $u$, whereas Theorem~10 of the cited work gives
    78	closeness only on average over $u$ \cite{Natarajan2017Linearity}.  The quotation
    79	also inserts $\delta\leq1$, which is absent from the provider theorem and would
    80	unnecessarily obstruct applying it with a fiber's actual defect.  The assertion
    81	at the identity follows from exact linearity as above.
    82	
    83	Lines~825--832 construct the family $O^{x,z,r,s}$ and establish approximate
    84	linearity only after averaging over $x,z,r,r',s,s'$.  They then apply the
    85	single-family theorem separately for every $(x,z)$ and state that sufficiently
    86	many zero ancillas avoid a further extension.  The remaining implicit step is
    87	to make the theorem's possibly fiber-dependent auxiliary spaces uniform.
    88	
    89	The finite setting admits a standard repair.  Apply the theorem on each fiber
    90	with its actual defect, choose one finite auxiliary space large enough for all
    91	returned spaces, and embed each returned space so that its unit vector maps to

    39	
    40	Let $H_X$ and $H_Z$ be the positive contractions of the extraction proof, and
    41	let $\vartheta$ be a unit vector such that
    42	\[
    43	  \langle\vartheta,H_W\vartheta\rangle\geq1-\delta/2
    44	  \qquad (W\in\{X,Z\}).
    45	\]
    46	Since $(I-H_W)^2\geq0$,
    47	\[
    48	  H_W^2\geq2H_W-I,
    49	  \qquad
    50	  \langle\vartheta,H_W^2\vartheta\rangle\geq1-\delta.
    51	\]
    52	Also $\lVert(I-H_W)\vartheta\rVert^2\leq\delta$, whence
    53	\[
    54	  \lVert H_X\vartheta-H_Z\vartheta\rVert^2\leq4\delta.
    55	\]
    56	Together with $H_XH_Z$ equal to the EPR projection, these estimates give the
    57	required overlap bound, with constants absorbed into the stated
    58	$O(\sqrt\delta)$ error.

    60	For the final transfer, let $\phi\colon\mathcal H\to\mathcal K$ be an isometry
    61	and set $Q=\phi\phi^\dagger$.  If $N_h$ is the unitary-conjugated extension of
    62	a measurement operator $M_h$, then the exact identity is
    63	\[
    64	  \phi M_h\phi^\dagger=N_hQ=QN_h,
    65	\]
    66	not merely $N_h$.  Thus comparison of $N_h$ with an ideal projector must be
    67	combined with control of $(I-Q)\Delta$ on the ideal comparison state
    68	$\Delta$.

\title{Documenting Possible Gaps, Counterexamples, and Formalization Deviations}
\author{}
\date{2026-04-29}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

\section{Purpose}

When a formalization relies on a cited mathematical source, the cited source
should remain intact.  It is a source, not an errata file.  If a possible gap,
missing hypothesis, incorrect numerical constant, or other mathematical
discrepancy is found, the matter should be recorded in a separate LaTeX note.
In this repository such notes live under \path{docs/paper-gaps/}.  The same
principle applies when the formal development has already diverged from the
cited source, for instance by changing a statement so that it compiles, or by
using a different mathematical route because an available formal-library theorem
has a slightly different form.  Such a note is a mathematical note first, and a
record of the formalization second: it should be readable by a mathematician or
mathematical physicist who has not followed the issue discussion.

The note should isolate the mathematical mechanism.  It should say what the
cited source asserts, what the cited results actually imply, where a term or
hypothesis is lost, and what statement the formal development proves instead.
If the formal proof takes a different route, the note should explain the
replacement argument and the hypotheses on which it rests.  This is especially
important when the proof uses a theorem, construction, or convention from
Mathlib which is not part of the cited argument.  In that case the note should
state the Mathlib result in ordinary mathematical language, explain how it is
specialized to the notation of the paper, and compare its hypotheses and
conclusion with the step it replaces.  It should not merely say that \Lean{} did
not accept a proof, that the modified proof compiles, or that a named library
lemma was applied.

The documents in this directory should themselves follow this standard.  A
policy or template which reads like a checklist will tend to produce checklist
notes; the examples and templates should therefore be written as mathematical
prose.

\section{Concision and Readability}

A paper-gap note should be short enough that a reader can understand the issue
in one sitting.  The first page should answer four questions: what the source
uses, how hard the remaining formal work is, what the formalization or audit
checked, and what the current verdict is.  Begin with a short
\emph{At a glance} section when the note concerns an open or recently resolved
formalization task.  That section should estimate the difficulty, the rough
implementation weight, the split between Mathlib reuse and project-local work,
and the key Mathlib APIs or modules.  Use honest ranges, not false precision.

The \emph{Key theorem forms} section should be Section~2, immediately after
\emph{At a glance}.  Put the theorem forms before the source details so the
reader knows what the formalization is aiming to prove.  After that, keep the
source assertion, the mechanism being checked, the blueprint/formal comparison,
and the conclusion.  Use more sections only when a counterexample or long
derivation genuinely needs room.

Keep background to the minimum needed for the local point.  Prefer one clear
special case over a general restatement of the surrounding theorem.  Use displayed
equations for the source assertion, the key calculation, and the theorem forms;
avoid displays for traceability data, declaration names, or long lists.  The
blueprint/formal comparison should be compact and should not repeat the theorem
forms.  The section ``Form of the Note'' below specifies where traceability data
belongs; the body should read as mathematical prose, not as a log.

If the verdict is that there is no mathematical discrepancy, say so plainly and
stop.  Keep the conclusion highly compact, normally under twenty source lines.
If the only remaining work is an implementation task, name it briefly and link
the issue or pull request in a footnote.

\section{When the Investigation Starts}

The investigation starts when the obstruction appears to be mathematical rather
than merely formal.  No final judgement is needed at this stage.  It is enough
that, after reading the relevant source and attempting the corresponding formal
statement, the proof seems to require a different scalar, an additional
hypothesis, a different tensor placement, a distinction between two objects which
the prose identifies, or an auxiliary assertion not supplied by the cited
argument.

The same investigation should also start when such a deviation is discovered
after the fact.  If the existing formal development or informal blueprint has
already changed the statement, strengthened a hypothesis, weakened a conclusion,
inserted an unadvertised lemma, or replaced the cited proof by a different
formal-library argument, the mathematical change should be documented even if all
relevant files already compile.

At this early stage the purpose is to preserve the question while it is still
local.  The note may later conclude that the matter is only notational, that an
intermediate estimate in the cited source needs a harmless correction, that a
missing hypothesis is genuinely needed, or that no discrepancy remains.  Thus
the trigger is not the severity of the eventual verdict, but the appearance of a
real mismatch between the cited reasoning and the statement that can be
formalized.

A failed tactic search, a missing formal lemma, or an inconvenient coercion is
not enough.  The obstruction must survive translation back into ordinary
mathematics.

Sometimes an investigation uncovers an improvement that is not a discrepancy:
the formalization works correctly, but it could be simplified by using an
existing library, replacing a custom type, or adopting a cleaner proof route.
These are not, by themselves, paper-gap notes.  They are action items.  When
such an improvement is identified, open a GitHub issue or pull request that
describes the proposed change.  If the investigation also produces a paper-gap
note, link the issue or pull request from that note: the note records the
mathematical justification, and the issue or pull request drives the
implementation.

\section{When to Write a Note}

A note should be written once the source argument and the formal proof no longer
match as mathematical arguments.  This includes, for instance, a numerical
estimate whose constant does not follow from the cited lemma, a displayed
conclusion which uses an unstated hypothesis, or a step in which two objects are
identified although they must remain distinct.  In analytic, algebraic,
probabilistic, or quantum arguments, such distinctions may concern the domain of
a map, the placement of a tensor factor, the type of an outcome, the distinction
between a structure and a substructure, or the scalar carried by an approximation
relation.

A note is required when an audit finds that a Lean declaration associated with a
source-labelled statement has acquired an extra non-source hypothesis, such as
bridge, residual, repair, producer, or obligation-structure data.  Such a
declaration is temporary proof debt, not a replacement for the source theorem,
and should not be introduced merely to avoid a \verb|sorry|.  The note must say
plainly that the Lean result is conditional, identify the source-faithful theorem
form that remains to be proved, and give the intended obligation discharger or
removal plan.  The blueprint should not mark the source-labelled statement with
\verb|\leanok| by pointing to this conditional helper.

Changing a Lean theorem away from the statement in
\path{references/ldt-paper/} is strongly discouraged.  A paper-gap note should
not make such a change look routine: it should explain the mathematical
necessity, or else classify the change as proof debt to be removed.

When an existing conditional helper is audited, the first task is to extract any
argument it already contains into source-faithful lemmas.  If the remaining
bridge hypothesis cannot be derived from the paper hypotheses, the formal
development should restore the source theorem statement and record the missing
proof obligation explicitly, rather than retaining the strengthened statement as
though it were the paper theorem.

This requirement is not meant to classify every explicit Lean side condition as
a discrepancy.  Positivity, nonemptiness, decidability, field-model instances,
and denominator nonvanishing hypotheses may be faithful encodings of the domain
in which the paper's theorem is stated.  The note should distinguish such
boundary hypotheses from hypotheses that supply an unproved step of the paper
argument.

A note is also appropriate when the proof becomes formal only after changing an
intermediate scalar, weakening a conclusion, strengthening a hypothesis, or
inserting an additional lemma which is not simply an expansion of the cited
argument.  These are mathematical changes, even when they are harmless for the
final theorem.  It is likewise appropriate when an available formal-library
theorem proves the needed result under a somewhat different formulation from the
cited source.  In that case the note should be deliberately pedagogical.  It
should explain, in ordinary mathematical language, what the replacement result
says, how it is specialized, which hypotheses are new or differently packaged,
and why the resulting statement is a legitimate substitute for the step in the
cited argument.  If the issue remains open after reasonable attempts, the note
should say what has been checked and what remains unknown.

\section{Counterexamples}

If the cited assertion appears to be false, the note should not stop at saying
that the proof cannot be formalized.  It should give the counterexample, or the
smallest relevant part of it, in ordinary mathematical notation.  The example
should be accompanied by enough verification that the reader can see both sides:
the hypotheses of the cited assertion hold, and its conclusion fails.

When feasible, the counterexample should also be formalized in \Lean{}.  This is
especially valuable when the example is finite, algebraic, computational, or
otherwise small enough that the failure can be checked without reproducing the
whole surrounding theory.  The note should then state the mathematical content
of the checked counterexample and identify the corresponding Lean declaration in
a footnote.  The Lean file is not a substitute for the prose: the prose should
still explain why the example refutes the cited assertion.

\section{Revision of a Note}

A paper-gap note may be provisional.  It may begin as soon as the mathematical
obstruction has been isolated well enough to state the question, and it may be
revised as the calculation, the blueprint, or the corresponding \Lean{}
declarations become clearer.  The first version need not know the final
classification, but it should say plainly which mathematical point is known and
which point remains unsettled.

Later revisions should not make the note into a chronological log.  They should
rewrite the document so that it remains a coherent account of the present
mathematical understanding.  If the verdict changes, the conclusion should state
the current verdict; the linked issue or pull request can preserve the earlier
discussion.

\section{Form of the Note}

Each note should stand on its own.  It should give the date, cite the relevant
source article, and provide enough traceability for the reader to locate the
original passage and the project discussion.  GitHub issues and pull requests may
be linked with \verb|\href|, and source files, line ranges, and labels should be
recorded when they help the reader check the claim.  These references should
serve the exposition rather than govern it: the main text should be organized
around the mathematical assertion and its proof.

The note should introduce its notation before using it.  Symbols for
measurements, tensor factors, approximation relations, and error parameters
should be named in prose.  If an approximation relation is state-dependent, the
state should be named, or its defining expression should be given when this can
be done briefly.  Only after the notation is in place should the note state the
assertion in the cited source, using a bibliographic citation such as
\verb|\cite[Section~...]{...}| when the section or chapter is known.

Only the relevant hypotheses should be reproduced.  If the question is a scalar
substitution, a missing term, or a missing hypothesis, the note should not quote
a long unrelated part of the proof.  It should give the cited lemma or
proposition in the special case actually used, then display the calculation or
logical implication in which the discrepancy appears.

Displayed equations should be used with restraint.  They are appropriate for the
source estimate being checked, the cited estimate in the form actually used, and
the calculation where a term or hypothesis appears or disappears.  When a
displayed equation is identified by a source label, the label should appear on
the right of the display, while the surrounding prose refers to the mathematical
assertion itself.  The standard \texttt{amsmath} command \verb|\tag| is the
right mechanism for this; a separate local convention should be introduced only
if the standard mechanism is genuinely insufficient.  For a multi-line aligned
display, tag the individual lines that carry the source information rather than
forcing a long combined label below the equations.  Short
scalar definitions and elementary inequalities should remain inline when the
sentence reads better that way.  As in ordinary mathematical writing, a displayed
formula is part of the surrounding sentence and should be punctuated accordingly.

+# Extraction by the swap unitaries
+
+The concrete swap operators below yield the Pauli extraction conclusion. The
+local maps are constructed from the global polynomial
+measurements, and all operators retain the heterogeneous Alice and Bob
+placements. The generalized Pauli projectors use the field and basis fixed by
+`P.model`.

+## References
+
+The extraction witness formalizes `lem:qld-unitary` in
+`blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:295-314`, from
+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1860`.
+The error-form comparison records `rem:pauli-robustness-form`, blueprint lines
+380-385 and paper lines 1855-1858 and 1868-1876.
+-/
+
+open scoped BigOperators Matrix

+namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
+
+open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum
+
+noncomputable section
+
+/-- The concrete conclusion of `lem:qld-unitary`: the two swap maps extract an
+EPR state and conjugate each player's total Pauli measurement to the canonical
+Pauli projectors. The answer sum in `pauli_close` is over
+`PauliRegister P`; the uniform distribution on `Unit` records that there is no
+average over questions.
+
+Blueprint `ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:295-314`; paper
+`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1685,1827-1859`. The swap maps
+are `swapUnitary w .alice` and `swapUnitary w .bob`, defined from the
+side-indexed global measurements, and use only the basis fixed by `P.model`.
+-/
+structure ExtractionWitness {P : AdmissibleParams} {epsilon deltaS : ℝ}
+    (S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon) (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaS)
+    (delta : ℝ) where
+  /-- Each swap map is a right unitary. -/
+  swap_right_unitary : ∀ side : PlayerSide,
+    swapUnitary w side * (swapUnitary w side)ᴴ = 1
+  /-- Each swap map is a left unitary. -/
+  swap_left_unitary : ∀ side : PlayerSide,
+    (swapUnitary w side)ᴴ * swapUnitary w side = 1
+  /-- The auxiliary state on registers `AA'BB'`. -/
+  aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ
+    (ExtractionAuxRegisters P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
+  /-- The auxiliary state is normalized. -/
+  aux_norm : ‖aux‖ = 1
+  /-- Applying both concrete swap maps to the expanded state extracts the ideal
+  auxiliary-state/EPR tensor product. -/
+  state_close :
+    ‖S.applyBoth (swapUnitary w .alice) (swapUnitary w .bob) S.psiHat -
+        S.idealExpState aux‖ ^ 2 ≤ delta
+  /-- On the ideal extracted state, conjugated total-Pauli effects are close to
+  the canonical projectors, for both players and both Pauli bases. -/
+  pauli_close : ∀ (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind),
+    opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution Unit)
+      (fun (_ : Unit) (h : PauliRegister P) =>
+        conjBy (S.placeSide side (swapUnitary w side))
+          (S.placePlayer side ((S.pauliMeas side W).effect h)))
+      (fun (_ : Unit) (h : PauliRegister P) =>
+        S.placeExtractedRegister side (pauliProj W h))
+      (S.idealExpState aux) ≤ delta
+

+explicit extraction scale applied to `deltaConstructPaulis`.

+    ∃ C : ℝ, 1 ≤ C ∧
+      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (epsilon deltaG : ℝ),
+        0 ≤ epsilon → epsilon ≤ 1 → 0 ≤ deltaG →
+          ∀ (S : ProjectiveSetting P epsilon)
+            (w : GlobalPairWitness S deltaG),

+    (hb : 0 < b) (hb1 : b < 1) :
+    ∃ a' b' : ℝ, 1 ≤ a' ∧ 0 < b' ∧ b' < 1 ∧
+      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (epsilon : ℝ), 0 ≤ epsilon →
+        epsilon ≤ 1 →
+        deltaExtract C
+            (deltaConstructPaulis C epsilon
+              (deltaQld a b epsilon P.m P.d P.q) P.m P.d P.q)
+            P.m P.d P.q ≤
+          deltaQld a' b' epsilon P.m P.d P.q := by

   324		In the source proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-unitary}, the triangle inequality gives $\| H_X \ket{\vartheta} - H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \| \leq \| (\Id - H_X)\ket{\vartheta} \| + \| (\Id - H_Z)\ket{\vartheta} \| \leq 2\sqrt{\delta_P}$, so that $\| H_X \ket{\vartheta} - H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \|^2 \leq 4\delta_P$; the source instead asserts the bound $2\sqrt{\delta_P}$ for the \emph{squared} norm, which holds only when $\sqrt{\delta_P} \leq 1/2$, and consequently carries the term $\sqrt{\delta_P}$ into an overlap bound of $1 - 2\delta_P - \sqrt{\delta_P}$. The proof above uses the corrected bound $4\delta_P$, which gives the overlap bound $1 - 4\delta_P$ and leaves the final bound $\delta_{\mathrm{qld}} = O(\delta_P^{1/4} + md/q)$ unchanged. The source proof also normalizes the vector $(\bra{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M})_{\mathrm{A}''\mathrm{B}''} \ket{\vartheta}$ without ensuring that it is nonzero; the case distinction on $\delta_P$ in the proof above supplies this, the conclusions of the lemma being trivial when $\delta_P$ exceeds a universal constant.
   325	\end{remark}

   327	\section{Proof of the soundness of the Pauli basis test}
   328	
   329	We can now prove the soundness theorem for the Pauli basis test, stated as Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli} in Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-test}.
   330	
   331	\begin{proof}
   332		\proves{thm:pauli}
   333		\uses{lem:qld-unitary, lem:pauli-completeness, thm:naimark, lem:projective-strategy-setup, def:expanded-state, def:EPR, def:povm-distance}
   334		Let $(\ket{\psi},M)$ be a strategy for $\mathfrak{G}^{\mathrm{Pauli}}_{(q,m,d)}$ that succeeds with probability at least $1 - \eps$, where $\ket{\psi}$ is a bipartite state on registers $\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathrm{B}$. By Naimark's theorem (Theorem~\ref{thm:naimark}, as formulated in~\cite[Theorem 5.1]{Ji2020LowIndividualDegree}), at the cost of extending $\ket{\psi}$ by sufficiently many ancilla qubits initialized in the state $\ket{0}$, we may assume that the strategy is projective and that the state is padded as in the conventions of Lemma~\ref{lem:projective-strategy-setup} and the convention following it. Let $V_{\mathrm{A}}$ be the unitary acting on registers $\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''$ given by Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-unitary}, and let $\phi_{\mathrm{A}}$ be the isometry mapping register $\mathrm{A}$ to registers $\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''$, where $\mathrm{A}'$ and $\mathrm{A}''$ are isomorphic to $(\C^q)^{\ot M}$, defined by
   335		\[
   336			\phi_{\mathrm{A}}\colon \ket{\theta}_{\mathrm{A}} \mapsto V_{\mathrm{A}} \bigl(\ket{\theta}_{\mathrm{A}} \ot (\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M})_{\mathrm{A}' \mathrm{A}''}\bigr)\;;
   337		\]
   338		define $\phi_{\mathrm{B}}$ analogously.
   339		% Reliance disclosure added: the proof chain of thm:pauli passes through
   340		% lem:qld-4-7, whose source proof (lines 1277--1413 of
   341		% 14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex) instantiates the classical low
   342		% individual degree test at dimension 2m+2 without a divisibility
   343		% hypothesis; the sentence below records the resulting outstanding
   344		% obligation.
   345		This invocation is where the analysis of the classical low individual degree test enters: Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-unitary} rests on the polynomial-pair measurement of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-7}, whose proof instantiates the classical test in $2m+2$ variables and at present does so only when $2m+2$ divides $q$ --- a divisibility that fails for every admissible tuple with $m \geq 2$. Three further steps of that same chain are likewise unproved. The classical soundness statement invoked there, Theorem~\ref{lem:ld-soundness}, is imported from Theorem~4.7 of~\cite{Ji2021Quantum} through an identification of the game $\mathfrak{G}^{\mathrm{ld}}_{(q,m,d,1)}$ with the two-prover tensor-code test for $\code^{\ot m}$, and neither that game correspondence nor the bound on the auxiliary parameter of Theorem~4.7 under which the stated error function $\delta_{\mathrm{ld}}$ is obtained has been established; both, with the divisibility obstruction, are documented in \cite{gap:qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility}. Furthermore, the combined-lines consistency of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-13}, which Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-7} consumes, is established here only with the error $m \cdot \poly(\eps, md/q)$, the error form $\poly(m^2 \eps, md/q)$ carried in its statement remaining unproved (see \cite{gap:qpbt_combined-lines-error-term}). The present proof is therefore complete only modulo these four obligations. Since the expanded state $\ket{\hat\psi}$ of Definition~\ref{def:expanded-state} is exactly $\ket{\psi}$ with the halves of $M$ pairs $\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}$ appended locally in registers $\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''$ and $\mathrm{B}'\mathrm{B}''$, we have $\phi_{\mathrm{A}} \ot \phi_{\mathrm{B}} \ket{\psi} = V_{\mathrm{A}} \ot V_{\mathrm{B}} \ket{\hat\psi}$. Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-unitary} therefore yields a state $\ket{\mathrm{aux}}$ on registers $\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'$ such that
   346		\[
   347			\bigl\| \phi_{\mathrm{A}} \ot \phi_{\mathrm{B}} \ket{\psi} - \ket{\mathrm{aux}} \ot \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M} \bigr\|^2 \leq \delta_{\mathrm{qld}}\;.
   348		\]
   349		% Transfer step added: the source (lines 1864--1875 of
   350		% 14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex) passes directly from the
   351		% conjugation estimates of lem:qld-unitary, which concern the
   352		% unitarily conjugated operators V (M_h ot Id) V^dagger, to the
   353		% corresponding estimates for the isometry phi, whose conjugation
   354		% inserts the projection onto its range; the range-projection
   355		% argument below supplies the missing step.
   356		Item~2 of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-unitary} concerns the unitarily conjugated operators $N^W_h = V_{\mathrm{A}} \, (M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h)_{\mathrm{A}} \, V_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger$, whereas conjugation by the isometry $\phi_{\mathrm{A}}$ additionally inserts the projection $Q_{\mathrm{A}} = \phi_{\mathrm{A}} \phi_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger = V_{\mathrm{A}} \, \bigl(\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}\bra{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}\bigr)_{\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''} \, V_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger$ onto the range of $\phi_{\mathrm{A}}$: since $(M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h)_{\mathrm{A}}$ and $\bigl(\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}\bra{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}\bigr)_{\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''}$ act on disjoint registers and hence commute,
   357		\[
   358			\phi_{\mathrm{A}} \, (M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h)_{\mathrm{A}} \, \phi_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger
   359			= V_{\mathrm{A}} \, \Bigl( (M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h)_{\mathrm{A}} \ot \bigl(\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}\bra{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}\bigr)_{\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''} \Bigr) \, V_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger
   360			= N^W_h \, Q_{\mathrm{A}} = Q_{\mathrm{A}} \, N^W_h\;.
   361		\]
   362		The estimates transfer from $N^W_h$ to $\phi_{\mathrm{A}} \, (M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h)_{\mathrm{A}} \, \phi_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger$ as follows. Write $\ket{\Delta} = \ket{\mathrm{aux}} \ot \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}$ and $\ket{\vartheta} = \phi_{\mathrm{A}} \ot \phi_{\mathrm{B}} \ket{\psi}$. Since $\phi_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger \phi_{\mathrm{A}} = \Id$, the projection $\Id - Q_{\mathrm{A}}$ annihilates $\ket{\vartheta}$, so the displayed bound above gives
   363		\[
   364			\bigl\| (\Id - Q_{\mathrm{A}}) \ket{\Delta} \bigr\|^2
   365			= \bigl\| (\Id - Q_{\mathrm{A}}) (\ket{\Delta} - \ket{\vartheta}) \bigr\|^2
   366			\leq \bigl\| \ket{\Delta} - \ket{\vartheta} \bigr\|^2
   367			\leq \delta_{\mathrm{qld}}\;.
   368		\]
   369		Since the strategy is projective, the operators $N^W_h$, for $h \in \F_q^M$, are mutually orthogonal projectors summing to the identity, so $\sum_h \| N^W_h \ket{\xi} \|^2 = \| \ket{\xi} \|^2$ for every vector $\ket{\xi}$. Decomposing
   370		\[
   371			\bigl( \phi_{\mathrm{A}} \, (M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h)_{\mathrm{A}} \, \phi_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger - (\tau^W_h)_{\mathrm{A}''} \bigr) \ket{\Delta}
   372			= \bigl( N^W_h - (\tau^W_h)_{\mathrm{A}''} \bigr) \ket{\Delta} - N^W_h (\Id - Q_{\mathrm{A}}) \ket{\Delta}
   373		\]
   374		and summing the squared norms over $h$ via $\| \xi - \xi' \|^2 \leq 2\|\xi\|^2 + 2\|\xi'\|^2$, the first terms contribute $O(\delta_{\mathrm{qld}})$ by Item~2 of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-unitary} and the second terms contribute at most $2 \| (\Id - Q_{\mathrm{A}}) \ket{\Delta} \|^2 \leq 2\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}$; hence, for $W \in \{X,Z\}$,
   375		\[
   376			\phi_{\mathrm{A}} \, (M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h)_{\mathrm{A}} \, \phi_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger \approx_{\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}} (\tau^W_h)_{\mathrm{A}''}
   377			\qquad \text{and, by the identical argument,} \qquad
   378			\phi_{\mathrm{B}} \, (M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h)_{\mathrm{B}} \, \phi_{\mathrm{B}}^\dagger \approx_{\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}} (\tau^W_h)_{\mathrm{B}''}\;,
   379		\]
   380		where the $\approx$ statements hold with respect to the state $\ket{\mathrm{aux}} \ot \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}$ and the answer summation is over $h \in \F_q^M$; the constant implicit in $\approx_{\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}}$ (Definition~\ref{def:povm-distance}) absorbs the factors accumulated above. This shows that the game $\mathfrak{G}^{\mathrm{Pauli}}_{(q,m,d)}$ is a self-test, with robustness $\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}(\eps,m,d,q)$, for the canonical Pauli strategy of Lemma~\ref{lem:pauli-completeness}. Identifying the registers $\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'$ with $\mathrm{A}'$ and $\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'$ with $\mathrm{B}'$ matches the statement of Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli}, in which $\phi_{\mathrm{A}}\colon \mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{A}} \to \mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{A}'} \ot \mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{A}''}$. Finally, unpacking the dependence on the parameters $\eps, m, d, q$, the function $\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}(\eps,m,d,q) = O(\delta_P^{1/4} + md/q)$ has the form $a(md)^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$ for universal constants $a > 1$ and $0 < b < 1$; here $\delta_P = C(\delta_G + \sqrt{\eps} + md/q)$ and $\delta_G$ already has that form. See Remark~\ref{rem:pauli-robustness-form} for the reconciliation with the statement of Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli}.
   381	\end{proof}
   382	
   383	\begin{remark}[Norm conventions in the robustness bound]\label{rem:pauli-robustness-form}
   384		The proof above, following the source, establishes the first conclusion of Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli} in the squared form $\| \phi_{\mathrm{A}} \ot \phi_{\mathrm{B}} \ket{\psi} - \ket{\mathrm{aux}} \ot \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M} \|^2 \leq \delta_{\mathrm{qld}}$, whereas the theorem bounds the unsquared norm by $\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}(\eps,m,d,q)$. The two are reconciled by replacing the exponent $b$ with $b/2$ and enlarging $a$, since the class of functions $a(md)^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$ is closed under square roots up to such adjustments of the universal constants. Similarly, the closing sentence of the source proof asserts constants $a > 1$ and $0 < b < 1$, while Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli} requires only $a \geq 1$ and $0 < b < 1$; the former implies the latter.
   385	\end{remark}

    19	\section{At a glance}
    20	
    21	\begin{itemize}
    22	  \item \textbf{Difficulty.} Medium.  The extraction proof contains two
    23	  incorrect numerical steps and later suppresses the range projection when
    24	  passing from unitary conjugation to isometry conjugation.
    25	  \item \textbf{Estimated weight.} A corrected positive-contraction estimate,
    26	  a small-error case split for normalization, and one range-projection transfer
    27	  lemma for a projective measurement family.
    28	  \item \textbf{Mathlib/project split.} Positivity, contraction inequalities,
    29	  isometry range projections, and norm estimates belong to finite-dimensional
    30	  Hilbert-space algebra.  The state-dependent family distance and register
    31	  placements are project-local.
    32	  \item \textbf{Key mathematical inputs.} The inequality
    33	  $H^2\geq2H-I$ for a positive contraction, the triangle inequality, and
    34	  $Q=\phi\phi^\dagger$ for an isometry.  The repair is tracked in
    35	  \ghissue{19}.
    36	\end{itemize}
    37	
    38	\section{Key theorem forms}
    39	
    40	Let $H_X$ and $H_Z$ be the positive contractions of the extraction proof, and
    41	let $\vartheta$ be a unit vector such that
    42	\[
    43	  \langle\vartheta,H_W\vartheta\rangle\geq1-\delta/2
    44	  \qquad (W\in\{X,Z\}).
    45	\]
    46	Since $(I-H_W)^2\geq0$,
    47	\[
    48	  H_W^2\geq2H_W-I,
    49	  \qquad
    50	  \langle\vartheta,H_W^2\vartheta\rangle\geq1-\delta.
    51	\]
    52	Also $\lVert(I-H_W)\vartheta\rVert^2\leq\delta$, whence
    53	\[
    54	  \lVert H_X\vartheta-H_Z\vartheta\rVert^2\leq4\delta.
    55	\]
    56	Together with $H_XH_Z$ equal to the EPR projection, these estimates give the
    57	required overlap bound, with constants absorbed into the stated
    58	$O(\sqrt\delta)$ error.
    59	
    60	For the final transfer, let $\phi\colon\mathcal H\to\mathcal K$ be an isometry
    61	and set $Q=\phi\phi^\dagger$.  If $N_h$ is the unitary-conjugated extension of
    62	a measurement operator $M_h$, then the exact identity is
    63	\[
    64	  \phi M_h\phi^\dagger=N_hQ=QN_h,
    65	\]
    66	not merely $N_h$.  Thus comparison of $N_h$ with an ideal projector must be
    67	combined with control of $(I-Q)\Delta$ on the ideal comparison state
    68	$\Delta$.
    69	
    70	\section{Numerical defects in the source proof}
    71	
    72	Lines~1715--1742 of
    73	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex}
    74	construct $H_X,H_Z$ and identify $H_XH_Z$ with the EPR projection.  The norm
    75	estimate at lines~1743--1750 gives
    76	$\lVert(I-H_W)\vartheta\rVert\leq\sqrt\delta$.  At lines~1753--1757 the
    77	source substitutes $\delta$ inside the reverse triangle inequality
    78	\cite[lines~1715--1783]{Ji2020MIPStar}.  That replacement is not valid for
    79	small $\delta$.  The desired lower bound on
    80	$\langle H_W^2\rangle$ follows directly from $H_W^2\geq2H_W-I$, as above.
    81	
    82	The triangle inequality yields
    83	\[
    84	  \lVert H_X\vartheta-H_Z\vartheta\rVert\leq2\sqrt\delta,
    85	\]
    86	so its square is at most $4\delta$.  Line~1761 instead bounds that square by
    87	$2\sqrt\delta$ without a stated restriction.  This inequality follows when
    88	$\delta\leq1/4$; for larger error the theorem is made trivial by enlarging the
    89	universal constant.  The same small-error split ensures that the projected
    90	vector defined at lines~1769--1773 is nonzero before it is normalized.  These
    91	are local numerical repairs and do not weaken the extraction conclusion.
    92	
    93	\section{The range-projection obligation}
    94	
    95	Lines~1827--1858 prove state-dependent closeness for the concrete operators
    96	obtained by conjugating the original measurement with the swap unitaries.
    97	Lines~1864--1875 then define isometries by adjoining EPR pairs and applying
    98	those unitaries, and immediately state the corresponding closeness for
    99	$\phi M_h\phi^\dagger$.  The omitted range projection makes this implication
   100	non-definitional \cite[lines~1827--1875]{Ji2020MIPStar}.
   101	
   102	Let $\Psi$ be the original state and suppose $\phi\Psi$ is close to the ideal
   103	state $\Delta$.  Since $Q\phi\Psi=\phi\Psi$ and $Q$ is a contraction, the
   104	triangle inequality bounds $(I-Q)\Delta$ by the state-extraction error.  Using
   105	$\phi M_h\phi^\dagger=N_hQ$, split
   106	\[
   107	  (N_hQ-T_h)\Delta
   108	  =(N_h-T_h)\Delta-N_h(I-Q)\Delta,
   109	\]
   110	where $T_h$ is the ideal Pauli projector.  Summing squared norms over $h$
   111	uses projectivity and orthogonality to keep the second term under control.
   112	The same argument is required for each player and each Pauli basis.
   113	
   114	This transfer is an open proof obligation for the next extraction stage.  It
   115	must be a theorem derived from the concrete swap unitaries, transformed-state
   116	estimate, and operator comparisons.  It must not be stored as a bridge field,
   117	residual assumption, or hypothesis of the source-labelled soundness theorem.
   118	
   119	\section{Blueprint and formalization status}
   120	
   121	The proof of the extraction lemma in
   122	\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex}, lines~267--274, uses the
   123	correct positive-contraction estimate and explicit small-error convention.
   124	Lines~299--330 isolate the range projection and give the transfer strategy.
   125	The chapter therefore preserves the source's state and observable conclusions
   126	while exposing the missing argument.  Stage~4.2 should provide only the
   127	concrete extraction data and comparison theorems; the range-projection lemma
   128	belongs to Stage~4.3.
   129	
   130	\section{Conclusion}
   131	
   132	The printed triangle calculation has repairable numerical errors, and the
   133	last passage from unitaries to isometries omits a genuine range-projection
   134	argument.  Neither defect is a counterexample to Pauli soundness.  The former
   135	is corrected by positive-contraction inequalities and a small-error split;
   136	the latter remains a named downstream proof obligation whose hypotheses are
   137	already supplied by the extraction lemma.

    19	\section{At a glance}
    20	
    21	\begin{itemize}
    22	  \item \textbf{Difficulty.} Low.  The source drops a nontrivial phase when the
    23	  two binary-basis indices are distinct.
    24	  \item \textbf{Estimated weight.} One exact multiplication calculation for
    25	  generalized Pauli observables; no robustness estimate changes.

    28	  project's phase convention are project-local.

    30	  relation and nondegeneracy of the trace pairing.  The local correction is

    34	\section{Key theorem forms}
    35	
    36	Let $e_1,\ldots,e_t$ be the fixed self-dual basis of $\mathbb F_q$ over
    37	$\mathbb F_2$.  With the phase convention of the source, generalized Pauli
    38	observables satisfy
    39	\[
    40	  \tau^X(a)\tau^Z(b)
    41	  =(-1)^{\operatorname{tr}(a\mathbin{\cdot}b)}
    42	   \tau^Z(b)\tau^X(a).
    43	\]
    44	Substituting $a=e_j\widetilde u$ and $b=e_{j'}\widetilde v$ gives the exact
    45	relation
    46	\[
    47	  \widetilde X^j(\widetilde u)\widetilde Z^{j'}(\widetilde v)
    48	  =(-1)^{\operatorname{tr}
    49	      (e_je_{j'}(\widetilde u\mathbin{\cdot}\widetilde v))}
    50	   \widetilde Z^{j'}(\widetilde v)\widetilde X^j(\widetilde u).
    51	\]
    52	This formula applies uniformly, whether or not $j=j'$.
    53	
    54	\section{The false dichotomy in the source}
    55	
    56	Lines~1438--1450 of
    57	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex}
    58	identify each extracted observable with a tensor product containing
    59	$\tau^W(e_j\widetilde u)$.  Lines~1451--1456 then claim that the extracted
    60	$X$- and $Z$-observables commute whenever $j\neq j'$
    61	\cite[lines~1438--1456]{Ji2020MIPStar}.  Self-duality gives only
    62	\[
    63	  \operatorname{tr}(e_je_{j'})=0 \qquad (j\neq j').
    64	\]
    65	It does not imply
    66	\[
    67	  \operatorname{tr}(e_je_{j'}s)=0
    68	  \qquad\text{for every }s\in\mathbb F_q.
    69	\]
    70	
    71	Indeed, for distinct $j,j'$, the element $c=e_je_{j'}$ is nonzero.  The trace
    72	pairing is nondegenerate, so there is an $s\in\mathbb F_q$ for which
    73	$\operatorname{tr}(cs)=1$.  Taking vectors whose first coordinates are $1$
    74	and $s$, with all remaining coordinates zero, gives
    75	$\widetilde u\mathbin{\cdot}\widetilde v=s$.  The two extracted observables
    76	then anticommute.  This is a counterexample to the printed cross-basis
    77	commutation assertion.
    78	
    79	When $\widetilde u\mathbin{\cdot}\widetilde v$ lies in the prime field, the
    80	printed distinction is recovered from self-duality.  The chapter quantifies
    81	over arbitrary vectors, however, so that special case does not repair its
    82	statement.
    83	
    84	\section{Blueprint and formalization status}
    85	
    86	The discussion following the product-form calculation in
    87	\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex}, lines~69--95, records
    88	the full phase and notes that the false dichotomy is not used later in the
    89	extraction argument.  A formal theorem may therefore retain the mathematically
    90	correct uniform phase relation with a \textbf{Local fix} marker.  It must not
    91	assert exact commutation merely from $j\neq j'$.
    92	
    93	This correction changes neither the definition of the extracted observables
    94	nor the source-faithful consistency and extraction conclusions.  It repairs an
    95	auxiliary algebraic assertion that is independent of the robustness estimates.
    96	
    97	\section{Conclusion}
    98	
    99	The source's cross-basis commutation claim is false for general
   100	$\widetilde u$ and $\widetilde v$.  The correct relation retains the phase
   101	$(-1)^{\operatorname{tr}(e_je_{j'}(\widetilde u\cdot\widetilde v))}$.
   102	Because the later argument does not invoke the false dichotomy, this is a
   103	local correction rather than an additional hypothesis on the extraction
   104	theorem.

    33	  consistency, and Schwartz--Zippel.  The correction is tracked in
    34	  \ghissue{19}.
    35	\end{itemize}
    36	
    37	\section{Key theorem forms}
    38	
    39	For a word $h\colon\{0,1\}^m\to\mathbb F_q$, let $g_h$ be its multilinear
    40	extension.  Define the chapter's decoder by
    41	\[
    42	  \operatorname{Dec}(g)(y)=g(y),
    43	  \qquad y\in\{0,1\}^m.
    44	\]
    45	Then
    46	\[
    47	  \operatorname{Dec}(g_h)=h
    48	  \quad\text{and}\quad
    49	  \operatorname{Dec}(g_h)\mathbin{\cdot}\operatorname{ind}_m(u)=g_h(u).
    50	\]
    51	More generally, the second identity holds for a polynomial outcome $g$ under
    52	the explicit hypothesis that $g$ belongs to the image of the encoding; no
    53	converse is asserted.
    54	
    55	For an arbitrary bounded individual-degree polynomial $g$, the Boolean values
    56	determine its multilinear interpolant, not necessarily $g$ itself.  The
    57	unrestricted identity
    58	\[
    59	  \operatorname{Dec}(g)\mathbin{\cdot}\operatorname{ind}_m(u)=g(u)
    60	\]
    61	is therefore false.
    62	
    63	\section{Counterexample and source comparison}
    64	
    65	The low-degree encoding is defined at lines~873--897 of
    66	\path{references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex}.  The general decoder at
    67	lines~917--924 retains evaluations lying in a chosen subset $H$; the extraction
    68	chapter instead specifies at lines~1419--1420 of
    69	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex} that the
    70	decoder returns all evaluations on the Boolean cube.  This is the specialization
    71	$H=\mathbb F_q$, rather than the Boolean-valued shorthand used earlier
    72	\cite[lines~873--924 and 1419--1420]{Ji2020MIPStar}.
    73	
    74	Take $m=1$, $d\geq2$, and a field of characteristic two with more than two
    75	elements.  For $g(x)=x^2$, the Boolean evaluations are $g(0)=0$ and $g(1)=1$.
    76	Consequently the decoder is the word whose multilinear extension is $x$.
    77	For any $u\notin\{0,1\}$ with $u^2\neq u$,
    78	\[
    79	  \operatorname{Dec}(g)\mathbin{\cdot}\operatorname{ind}_1(u)=u
    80	  \neq u^2=g(u).
    81	\]
    82	Thus the equality asserted for every $g$ at lines~1483--1492 of the chapter-14
    83	source mirror is false \cite[lines~1483--1492]{Ji2020MIPStar}.  If degrees at
    84	least $q$ are allowed, equality as a function would not by itself prove encoding
    85	membership either, since $x^q$ and $x$ induce the same function on $\mathbb F_q$.
    86	
    87	\section{Required repair}
    88	
    89	The extraction proof must split the marginal measurement into encoding and
    90	non-encoding outcomes.  On encoding outcomes, the restricted identity above
    91	justifies the substitution.  On the complement, the proof must bound
    92	\[
    93	  \sum_{g\ \mathrm{not\ an\ encoding}}
    94	  \langle\widehat\psi,\widehat S_g^W\widehat\psi\rangle.
    95	\]
    96	The blueprint derives an $O(\delta_S)+md/q$ bound from point consistency and
    97	the combined point measurement.  A non-encoding polynomial differs from every
    98	encoded polynomial, so Schwartz--Zippel bounds the probability that their
    99	evaluations coincide.  This estimate is the open reduction; it must be proved
   100	from the paper hypotheses rather than inserted as an extraction hypothesis.
   101	
   102	The conjugation calculation at lines~1805--1822 does not require the false
   103	unrestricted identity.  Its decoder term cancels against the outcome shift,
   104	and only linearity of $h\mapsto g_h$ and the genuine identity
   105	$\operatorname{Dec}(g_h)=h$ are needed
   106	\cite[lines~1805--1822]{Ji2020MIPStar}.
   107	
   108	\section{Blueprint and formalization status}
   109	
   110	The decoding-identity remark and the proof of the pulled-apart consistency
   111	lemma in
   112	\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex} state the restricted
   113	identity and isolate the non-encoding-mass estimate.  The Lean API should
   114	therefore require encoding membership at every use of the dot-product
   115	evaluation theorem.  No unrestricted theorem, residual assumption, or witness
   116	field is source-faithful.
   117	
   118	\section{Conclusion}
   119	
   120	The decoding identity is false for a general polynomial outcome.  Restricting
   121	it to the encoding image is a necessary local correction.  Recovering the
   122	source's measurement-consistency conclusion then requires the separate
   123	non-encoding-mass estimate, which remains an open proof obligation.
   124	
   125	\bibliographystyle{alpha}
   126	\bibliography{references}
   127	
   128	\end{document}

    38	\section{Key theorem forms}
    39	
    40	Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, let $\rho$ be an arbitrary
    41	density operator on $H$, and let $u\mapsto O^u$ be binary observables on $H$,
    42	indexed by $\mathbb F_2^t$.  The cited theorem assumes the averaged
    43	correlation estimate
    44	\[
    45	  \mathop{\mathbb E}_{u,v}
    46	  \operatorname{Tr}\!\left(O^u O^v O^{u+v}\rho\right) \geq 1-\delta.
    47	\]
    48	It produces an auxiliary space $H'$, a unit vector $\mathrm{anc}\in H'$, and
    49	binary observables $L^u$ on $H\otimes H'$ satisfying, with
    50	$\rho'=\rho\otimes|\mathrm{anc}\rangle\langle\mathrm{anc}|$,
    51	\[
    52	  L^uL^v=L^{u+v}
    53	  \quad\text{for every }u,v.
    54	\]
    55	Moreover,
    56	\[
    57	  \mathop{\mathbb E}_{u}
    58	  \operatorname{Tr}\!\left((L^u-O^u\otimes I_{H'})^\dagger
    59	    (L^u-O^u\otimes I_{H'})\,\rho'\right)\leq\delta.
    60	\]
    61	In particular, $L^0=I$: exact linearity gives $(L^0)^2=L^0$, while an
    62	observable is invertible.

    64	The chapter needs a parameterized version.  For each pair $(x,z)$ it applies
    65	the theorem to $(r,s)\mapsto O^{x,z,r,s}$.  Since the provider theorem accepts
    66	the actual nonnegative defect on each fiber, no assumption that a fiber defect
    67	is at most one, and no good--bad fiber split, is needed.  One must still
    68	formulate the finite common-extension step that makes the auxiliary space

   832	\subsection{Polynomials and the low-degree code}
   833	\label{sec:ld-encoding}
   834	
   835	In this section, we introduce some basic definitions about polynomials over finite fields. 
   836	An $m$-variate polynomial $f$ over $\F_q$ is a function of the form
   837	\[
   838		f(x_1,\ldots,x_m) = \sum_{\alpha \in \{0,1,\ldots,q-1\}^m} c_\alpha
   839	  x_1^{\alpha_1} \cdots x_m^{\alpha_m}
   840	\]
   841	where $\{c_\alpha\}$ is a collection of coefficients in $\F_q$.
   842	We say that $f$ has \emph{individual degree (at most) $d$} if $c_\alpha\neq 0$ only if
   843	$\alpha_i \leq d $ for all $1\leq i\leq m$, and that it has \emph{total degree
   844	  (at most) $d$} if $c_\alpha\neq 0$ only if $\sum_i \alpha_i \leq d$.
   845	(Affine) \emph{multilinear} polynomials are polynomials with individual degree
   846	$1$.
   847	
   848	Low-degree polynomials play an important role in this paper.
   849	For one, the classical and quantum low-degree tests of \Cref{sec:ldt} are
   850	nonlocal games that efficiently certify that the players' answers are consistent
   851	with low-degree polynomials.
   852	Low-degree polynomials are also crucial in the probabilistically checkable
   853	proofs (PCP) construction that are used in ``answer reduction'' transformation
   854	(\Cref{sec:ans}).
   855	
   856	We recall the Schwartz-Zippel lemma: 
   857	
   858	\begin{lemma}[Schwartz-Zippel lemma~\cite{Sch80,Zip79}]
   859	  \label{lem:schwartz-zippel}
   860	  Let $f, g: \F_q^m \to \F_q$ be two unequal polynomials with total degree at most $d$. Then
   861	  \begin{equation*}
   862	    \Pr_{x \sim \F_q^m}[f(x) = g(x)] \leq d/q\;.
   863	  \end{equation*}
   864	\end{lemma}
   865	
   866	
   867	\paragraph{The low-degree code.}
   868	The Schwartz-Zippel lemma implies that the set of low-degree polynomials form an
   869	error-correcting code with good distance, which we call the \emph{low-degree
   870	  code}.\footnote{It is also known as the \emph{generalized Reed-Muller code} in
   871	  the coding theory literature.}
   872	
   873	Fix an integer $m \in \N$ and let $M = 2^m$.
   874	For every $y \in \{0,1\}^m$ define the following $m$-variate multilinear
   875	polynomial over $\F_q$:
   876	\[
   877		\ind_{m,y}(x) = \prod_{i: y_i = 1} x_i \cdot \prod_{i: y_i = 0} (1 - x_i) \;.
   878	\]
   879	Here, we identify $\{0,1\}$ as a subset of $\F_q$.
   880	Notice that, when restricted to the subcube $\{0,1\}^m$, $\ind_{m, y}$ is zero
   881	everywhere except for when $x = y$.
   882	For $a\in \F_q^M$, label the coordinates of $a$ as $a_y$ for $y\in \{0,1\}^m$
   883	(identifying the latter set with $\{1,\ldots,M\}$ using, say, the lexicographic
   884	ordering on strings).
   885	For any such $a$ define the multilinear polynomial $g_a: \F_q^m \to \F_q$,
   886	called the \emph{low-degree encoding of $a$}, as follows:
   887	\begin{equation}
   888	\label{eq:ld-encoding}
   889		 g_a(x) = \sum_{y \in \{0,1\}^m} a_y \cdot \ind_{m,y}(x)\;.
   890	\end{equation}
   891	Note that for any $y \in \{0,1\}^m$, $g_a(y) = a_y$.
   892	Furthermore, the map $a\mapsto g_a$ is linear: for every $x \in \F_q^m$,
   893	\begin{equation}
   894	\label{eq:low-degree-encoding-definition}
   895		g_a(x) = a \cdot \ind_m(x)\;,
   896	\end{equation}
   897	where $\ind_m(x)$ is the vector $(\ind_{m,y}(x))_{y \in \{0,1\}^m}\in\F_q^M$.
   898	
   899	\begin{lemma}
   900	\label{lem:ld-encoding-complexity}
   901	Let $q$ be an admissible field size, and let $M = 2^m$ for some integer $m$.
   902	The complexity of computing the evaluation of the low-degree encoding $g_a(x)$,
   903	given $a \in \F_q^M$ and $x \in \F_q^m$ represented in binary, is $\poly(M,\log
   904	q)$.
   905	\end{lemma}
   906	\begin{proof}
   907		Computing $g_a(x)$ requires computing the sum of products $a_y \cdot
   908	  \ind_{m,y}(x)$ over all $y \in \{0,1\}^m$.
   909	  Via \Cref{lem:efficient_arithmetic}, evaluating $\ind_{m,y}(x)$ takes time
   910	  $\poly(m,\log q)$ because it requires performing $m$ multiplications of $\F_q$
   911	  elements, and therefore the product $a_y \cdot \ind_{m,y}(x)$ requires
   912	  $\poly(m,\log q)$ time.
   913	  Computing the sum over all $y \in \{0,1\}^m$ requires $M \cdot \poly(m,\log q)
   914	  = \poly(M,\log q)$ time, as claimed.
   915	\end{proof}
   916	
   917	Finally, for any $H \subseteq \F_q$ we define the \emph{decoding} map
   918	$\coded_H(\cdot)$ which takes as input a polynomial $g : \F_q^m \to \F_q$ and
   919	returns the following vector $a \in \F_q^M$: for all $y \in \{0,1\}^m$, if $g(y)
   920	\in H$, then set $a_y = g(y)$, and otherwise set $a_y = 0$.
   921	Note that for all $a \in H^M$ we have $\coded_H(g_a) = a$ where $g_a$ is the
   922	low-degree encoding of $a$.
   923	For notational brevity we often write $\coded(\cdot)$ to denote the boolean
   924	decoding map $\coded_{\{0,1\}}(\cdot)$.

  1419	Recall the decoding map of the low-degree code defined in \Cref{sec:ld-encoding}. This map takes in a polynomial $g \in \ideg_{d,m}(\F_q)$ and returns a string $\coded(g) \in \F_q^{\nqubits}$ consisting of the evaluations of $g$ on the points in the hypercube $\{0,1\}^m$.
  1420	We now use this decoding map to construct a new set of measurement operators out of $\hat{S}$.
  1421	First, we introduce some notation. For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$ and all degree $d$ polynomials $g: \F_q^m \to \F_q$ define projectors
  1422	\[ \hat{S}^X_g = \sum_{g_\zpt} \hat{S}_{g,g_\zpt} \quad  \text{and}  \quad \hat{S}^Z_g = \sum_{g_\xpt} \hat{S}_{g_\xpt,g}\;,\]
  1423	where the measurement $\{\hat{S}_{g_\xpt,g_\zpt} \}$  is given by \Cref{lem:qld-4-7}.
  1424	
  1425	For all $W \in \{X, Z\}$, $\tilde{u} \in \F_q^{\nqubits}$, and $a \in \F_q$, define the projector
  1426	\begin{equation}\label{eq:def-tauwu}
  1427	 \tau^{W}_{a}(\tilde{u}) = \sum_{h \in \F_q^{\nqubits} \,:\, h \cdot \tilde{u} = a} \tau^W_{h}
  1428	\end{equation}
  1429	where recall that $\tau^W_h$ is the projector corresponding to measuring $(\C^q)^{\otimes \nqubits}$ in the $W$ basis and obtaining $h \in \F_q^\nqubits$ as the outcome. For all $\tilde{u} \in \F_q^\nqubits$ define the projective measurement $\{ \tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a \}_{a \in \F_q}$ by 
  1430		\begin{equation}
  1431		\label{eq:tilde_M}
  1432		\tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a =  \sum_{g} \hat{S}^W_g \otimes \tau_{(\coded(g) \cdot \tilde{u}) - a}^W(\tilde{u})\;.
  1433		\end{equation}
  1434		If $\hat{S}^W_g$ is viewed as an operator acting on registers $\alice \alice'$ (resp. $\bob \bob'$) then we view $\tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a$ as an operator acting on registers $\alice \alice' \alice''$ (resp. $\bob \bob' \bob''$). (When necessary we will indicate via subscripts which registers the operators are acting on.)
  1435	The $\tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a$ are projective because the $\hat{S}^W_g$ and $\tau^W$ operators are projective.
  1436	
  1437	
  1438		For all $j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}$ define the observable
  1439		\begin{equation}\label{eq:def-tildewj}
  1440			\tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) = \sum_a (-1)^{\tr(e_j a)} \, \tilde{M}_a^{W,\tilde{u}} \;,
  1441		\end{equation}
  1442		where $\{e_j\}_{j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}}$ denotes the self-dual basis for $\F_q$ over $\F_2$ specified in \Cref{sec:subfields}. Let $\tau^W$ be the generalized Pauli observable defined in Section~\ref{sec:generalized-pauli}. Observe that
  1443		\begin{align*}
  1444		\Big ( \sum_{g_\xpt,g_\zpt} (-1)^{\tr(e_j (\coded(g_W) \cdot \tilde{u}))} \hat{S}_{g_\xpt,g_\zpt} \Big ) \otimes \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u})
  1445		&= \sum_{g_\xpt,g_\zpt} \sum_h (-1)^{\tr(e_j (\coded(g_W) \cdot \tilde{u}))} (-1)^{\tr(e_j(\tilde{u} \cdot h))} \hat{S}_{g_\xpt,g_\zpt} \otimes \tau^W_h\\
  1446		&= \sum_{g_W} \sum_a  (-1)^{\tr(e_j (\tilde{u} \cdot\coded(g_W) + a))} \hat{S}_{g_W}^W \otimes \Big( \sum_{h:\, h\cdot \tilde{u} = a}\tau^W_h\Big)\\
  1447			&= \sum_{g_W} \sum_a  (-1)^{\tr(e_j (\tilde{u} \cdot\coded(g_W) + a))} \hat{S}_{g_W}^W \otimes \tau^W_a(\tilde{u})\\
  1448			&= 		\tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \;,
  1449		\end{align*}
  1450		where the first equality uses the definition of $\tau^W(e_j \tilde{u})$, the second uses the definition of $\hat{S}^W_{g_W}$ and regroups terms, the third uses the definition~\eqref{eq:def-tauwu} of $\tau^W_a(\tilde{u})$, and the last is by a change of variables. These equations in particular show that the observable $\tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u})$ is Hermitian and squares to the identity, because the measurement $\{ \hat{S}_{g_\xpt,g_\zpt} \}$ is projective. 
  1451		Furthermore, it can be verified by direct calculation that the observables $\tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u})$ satisfy the same relations as the generalized Pauli group. Specifically, for all $j,j' \in \{1,\ldots,t\}$, $\tilde{u}, \tilde{v} \in \F_q^\nqubits$,
  1452		\[
  1453			\tilde{X}^j(\tilde{u}) \tilde{Z}^{j'}(\tilde{v}) = \begin{cases}
  1454			\tilde{Z}^{j'}(\tilde{v}) \tilde{X}^j(\tilde{u})  & \qquad j \neq j' \\
  1455			(-1)^{\tr((e_j \tilde{u}) \cdot (e_j \tilde{v}))} \tilde{Z}^{j}(\tilde{v}) \tilde{X}^j(\tilde{u}) & \qquad j = j'
  1456			\end{cases}~.
  1457		\]
  1458		The next lemma shows that the measurements $\{ \tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a \}$  and observables $\tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u})$  are consistent with the original points measurements, and are self-consistent.
