  1463	\begin{lemma}
  1464	  \label{lem:qld-construct-the-paulis}
  1465	Let $\delta_S$ as in Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-7}.
  1466	For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$, all $\tilde{u} \in \F_q^\nqubits$ and $j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}$, the measurements $\{ \tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a \}_{a \in \F_q}$ and observables $\tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u})$ satisfy the following properties:
  1467	\begin{enumerate}
  1468	\item (\textbf{Consistency with points measurements}) For all $W \in \{X,Z\}$, for all $j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}$, and on average over uniformly random $u \in \F_q^m$,
  1469		\[
  1470			\Id_{\alice \alice' \alice''} \otimes \tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a \simeq_{\delta_S} M^{(\Point,W),u}_a \otimes \Id_{\bob \bob' \bob''}
  1471		\]
  1472		and
  1473		\[
  1474			\tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a \otimes \Id_{\bob \bob' \bob''} \simeq_{\delta_S} \Id_{\alice \alice' \alice''} \otimes M^{(\Point,W),u}_a \;.
  1475		\]	
  1476		\item (\textbf{Self-consistency}) On average over uniformly random $\tilde{u} \in \F_q^\nqubits$,
  1477		\[
  1478			\tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \otimes \Id_{\bob \bob' \bob''} \approx_{\delta_S} \Id_{\alice \alice' \alice''} \otimes \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u})\,.
  1479		\]
  1480	\end{enumerate}
  1481	\end{lemma}
  1482	
  1483	\begin{proof}
  1484	We show the first item of the lemma for the case when $M^{(\Point,W),u}_a$ acts on register $\alice$ and $\tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a$ acts on registers $\bob \bob' \bob''$ (the argument for when the $\alice$ and $\bob$ registers are interchanged proceeds analogously):
  1485		\begin{align*}
  1486			&\E_{u \in \F_q^m} \sum_a \bra{\hat{\psi}} M^{(\Point,W),u}_a \otimes \tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a \ket{\hat{\psi}} \\
  1487			&= \E_{u \in \F_q^m} \sum_{g,a} \bra{\hat{\psi}} (M^{(\Point,W),u}_a)_{\alice} \otimes (\hat{S}^W_g)_{\bob \bob'} \otimes (\tau^W_{\coded(g) \cdot \ind_m(u) -a}(\ind_m(u)))_{\bob''} \ket{\hat{\psi}} \\
  1488			&= \E_{u \in \F_q^m} \sum_{g} \bra{\hat{\psi}} (\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{\coded(g) \cdot \ind_m(u)})_{\alice \bob''} \otimes (\hat{S}^W_g)_{\bob \bob'} \ket{\hat{\psi}} \\
  1489			&= \E_{u \in \F_q^m} \sum_{g} \bra{\hat{\psi}} (\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{g(u)})_{\alice \bob''} \otimes (\hat{S}^W_g)_{\bob \bob'} \ket{\hat{\psi}} \\
  1490			&\geq 1 - \delta_S\;.
  1491		\end{align*}
  1492		The second line follows from expanding the definition of $\tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a$ using~\eqref{eq:tilde_M}, the third line follows from the definition of $\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_a$ given in Section~\ref{sec:expanding}, the fourth line follows from the fact that $\coded(g) \cdot \ind_m(u) = g(u)$, and the fifth line follows from \Cref{lem:qld-4-7}. This implies the first item of the Lemma.
  1493	
  1494	
  1495	To show the second item we first argue that, on average over $\tilde{u}$, 
  1496		\begin{equation}
  1497			\label{eq:qld-pulling-cons}
  1498			\Big ( \tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a \Big)_{\alice \alice' \alice''} \approx_{\delta_S} \Big ( \tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a \Big)_{\bob \bob' \bob''}.
  1499		\end{equation}
  1500		This follows because on average over $u \in \F_q^m$ and $\tilde{u} \in \F_q^\nqubits$ we have
  1501		\begin{align}
  1502			&\Big ( \tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a \Big)_{\alice \alice' \alice''} \label{eq:qld-pulling-0} \\
  1503			\approx_{\delta_S}& \Big ( \tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a \Big)_{\alice \alice'\alice''} \cdot \Big ( \sum_g (\hat{S}^W_g)_{\alice \alice'} \otimes  (\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{g(u)})_{\bob \alice''} \Big) \label{eq:qld-pulling-1} \\
  1504			=_{\phantom{\delta_S}}& \sum_g \Big ( (\hat{S}^W_g)_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\tau^W_{(\coded(g) \cdot \tilde{u}) - a}(\tilde{u}))_{\alice''} \Big) \cdot \Big(\sum_{r,s: r + s = g(u)} (M^{(\Point,W),u}_r)_{\bob} \otimes (\tau_s^W(\ind_m(u)))_{\alice''} \Big) \label{eq:qld-pulling-2} \\
  1505			=_{\phantom{\delta_S}}& \sum_{\substack{g,h: \\ (\coded(g)-h)\cdot \tilde{u} = a}}  (\hat{S}^W_g)_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\tau^W_h)_{\alice''} \otimes (M^{(\Point,W),u}_{(g-g_h)(u)})_{\bob}~. \label{eq:qld-pulling-2b}
  1506		\end{align}
  1507		The first inequality follows from right-multiplying~\eqref{eq:qld-pulling-0} by the approximation~\eqref{eq:qld-sg-cons} in \Cref{lem:qld-constructing-the-paulis-helper} (to be proved below) and using Fact~\ref{fact:add-a-proj}. Line~\eqref{eq:qld-pulling-2} follows from expanding the definition of $\tilde{M}^{W,\tilde{u}}_a$.  To obtain Line~\eqref{eq:qld-pulling-2b}, we expanded the definitions of $\tau^W_{(\coded(g) \cdot \tilde{u}) - a}(\tilde{u})$ and $\tau^W_s(\ind_m(u))$ using~\cref{eq:def-tauwu}, and the fact that $h \cdot \ind_m(u) = g_h(u)$ (due to \cref{eq:low-degree-encoding-definition}). Thus for all $g \in \ideg_{d,m}(\F_q)$ and $s \in \F_q$ we have
  1508		\[
  1509			\tau^W_{(\coded(g) \cdot \tilde{u}) - a}(\tilde{u}) \cdot \tau^W_s(\ind_m(u)) = \sum_{\substack{h: \\ (\coded(g) - h) \cdot \tilde{u} = a \\ g_h(u) = s}} \tau^W_h~.
  1510		\]
  1511	
  1512	
  1513		Using the self-consistency of $\{M^{(\Point,W),u}_a\}$ shown in Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-win-implications}, we then obtain
  1514		\begin{align}
  1515			\text{\eqref{eq:qld-pulling-2b}} &\approx_{\eps} \sum_{\substack{g,h: \\ (\coded(g)-h)\cdot \tilde{u} = a}} (\hat{S}^W_g)_{\alice \alice'} \cdot \Big((M^{(\Point,W),u}_{(g-g_h)(u)})_{\alice} \otimes (\tau_h^W)_{\alice''} \Big) \cdot \Big ( M^{(\Point,W),u}_{(g-g_h)(u)} \Big)_{\bob} \label{eq:qld-pulling-3} \\
  1516			&\approx_{0}\sum_{\substack{g,h: \\ (\coded(g)-h)\cdot \tilde{u} = a}} (\hat{S}^W_g)_{\alice \alice'} \cdot \Big((M^{(\Point,W),u}_{(g-g_h)(u)})_{\alice} \otimes (\tau_h^W)_{\alice'} \otimes (\tau_h^W)_{\alice''} \Big) \cdot \Big ( M^{(\Point,W),u}_{(g-g_h)(u)} \Big)_{\bob} \label{eq:qld-pulling-3a} \\
  1517			&= \sum_{\substack{g,h: \\ (\coded(g)-h)\cdot \tilde{u} = a}} (\hat{S}^W_g)_{\alice \alice'} \cdot \Big((\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{g(u)})_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\tau_h^W)_{\alice''} \Big) \cdot \Big ( M^{(\Point,W),u}_{(g-g_h)(u)} \Big)_{\bob} \;. \label{eq:qld-pulling-3b}
  1518		\end{align}
  1519		The ``$\approx_0$'' in Line~\eqref{eq:qld-pulling-3a} indicates that the left hand side is equal to the right hand side when applied to the state $\ket{\hat{\psi}}$. Line~\eqref{eq:qld-pulling-3a} follows from the self-consistency of the operators $\{\tau^W_h\}$, and Line~\eqref{eq:qld-pulling-3b} follows from the definition of $\{ \hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_a\}$. Using the fact that $\ket{\hat{\psi}} = \sum_{h'} (\tau^W_{h'})_{\bob'} \otimes (\tau^W_{h'})_{\bob''} \ket{\hat{\psi}}$, we get that 
  1520		\begin{align}
  1521		\text{\eqref{eq:qld-pulling-3b}} & \approx_0 \sum_{\substack{g,h: \\ (\coded(g)-h)\cdot \tilde{u} = a}} \Big((\hat{S}^W_g \cdot \hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{g(u)})_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\tau_h^W)_{\alice''} \Big) \cdot \Big( M^{(\Point,W),u}_{(g-g_h)(u)} \otimes \sum_{h'} \tau_{h'}^W \otimes \tau_{h'}^W\Big)_{\bob \bob' \bob''} \label{eq:qld-pulling-4} \\
  1522			&= \sum_{\substack{g,h,h': \\ (\coded(g)-h)\cdot \tilde{u} = a}} \Big((\hat{S}^W_g \cdot \hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{g(u)})_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\tau_h^W)_{\alice''} \Big) \cdot \Big( (\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{(g-g_h+g_{h'})(u)})_{\bob \bob'} \otimes (\tau_{h'}^W)_{\bob''} \Big) \;. \label{eq:qld-pulling-5}
  1523	\end{align}
  1524		Line~\eqref{eq:qld-pulling-5} follows from~\eqref{eq:qld-pulling-4} by expanding the definition of $\{ \hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_a\}$. Next, we argue that, on average over $u \in \F_q^m$,
  1525	\begin{align}
  1526			\text{\eqref{eq:qld-pulling-5}} &\approx_{\delta_S} \sum_{\substack{g,h,h': \\ (\coded(g)-h)\cdot \tilde{u} = a}} \Big((\hat{S}^W_g)_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\tau_h^W)_{\alice''} \Big) \otimes \Big( (\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{(g-g_h+g_{h'})(u)})_{\bob \bob'} \otimes (\tau_{h'}^W)_{\bob''} \Big)~. \label{eq:qld-pulling-7}
  1527			\end{align}
  1528			We show this by bounding the magnitude of the difference. Using the fact that $\hat{S}^W_g$ and $\tau^W_h$ are projective, we have:
  1529			\begin{align}
  1530			&\E_u \sum_a \Big \|\sum_{\substack{g,h,h': \\ (\coded(g)-h)\cdot \tilde{u} = a}} (\hat{S}^W_g \cdot (\Id - \hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{g(u)}))_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\tau_h^W)_{\alice''} \otimes (\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{(g-g_h+g_{h'})(u)})_{\bob \bob'} \otimes (\tau_{h'}^W)_{\bob''} \, \ket{\hat{\psi}} \Big \|^2 \notag \\
  1531	      =& \E_u \sum_{\substack{g,h,h'}} \bra{\hat{\psi}} \Big(((\Id - \hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{g(u)}) \cdot \hat{S}^W_g \cdot (\Id - \hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{g(u)}))_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\tau_h^W)_{\alice''} \Big) \notag \\
  1532	      & \hspace{20em} \cdot \Big( (\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{(g-g_h+g_{h'})(u)})^2_{\bob \bob'} \otimes (\tau_{h'}^W)_{\bob''} \Big) \ket{\hat{\psi}} \notag \\
  1533			\leq& \E_u \sum_{g} \bra{\hat{\psi}} ((\Id - \hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{g(u)}) \cdot \hat{S}^W_g \cdot (\Id - \hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{g(u)}))_{\alice \alice'} \ket{\hat{\psi}}\label{eq:qld-pulling-8} \\

  1537			Next, we show that on average over $u \in \F_q^m$,
  1538			\begin{align}

  1544			Before we justify the sequence of steps to go from Line~\eqref{eq:qld-pulling-7} to Line~\eqref{eq:qld-pulling-12}, we first argue how this establishes Line~\eqref{eq:qld-pulling-cons}, and hence the second item of the Lemma statement.

  1558			\paragraph{The approximation in Line~\eqref{eq:qld-pulling-10}.} The approximation in Line~\eqref{eq:qld-pulling-10} follows by bounding the magnitude of the difference:

  1568	The approximation in Line~\eqref{eq:qld-pulling-13} follows from the following calculation:

  1584	The inequality in Line~\eqref{eq:qld-pulling-14} follows from \Cref{eq:qld-s-point-con-bob} of \Cref{lem:qld-4-7}. This concludes the derivation of the approximation in Line~\eqref{eq:qld-pulling-10}.

  1586	\paragraph{The approximation in Line~\eqref{eq:qld-pulling-11}.} We establish this approximation by bounding the magnitude of the difference:
  1587	\begin{align*}
  1588		&\E_u \sum_a \Big \| \sum_{\substack{g,h,g',h': \\ (g' - g_{h'})(u) = (g -g_h)(u) \\ (\coded(g)-h)\cdot \tilde{u} = a}} \Big((\hat{S}^W_g)_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\tau_h^W)_{\alice''} \Big) \cdot \Big( (\hat{S}^W_{g'} \cdot (\Id - \hat{M}^{(\Point,W),u}_{g'(u)}))_{\bob \bob'} \otimes (\tau_{h'}^W)_{\bob''} \Big) \ket{\hat{\psi}} \Big \|^2 \\

  1597	\begin{align*}

  1609	We now give a proof of the following Lemma, which was used in several derivations in \Cref{lem:qld-construct-the-paulis}. 
  1610	\begin{lemma}
  1611	\label{lem:qld-constructing-the-paulis-helper}

  1618		\begin{gather}
  1619			\label{eq:qld-sg-cons2}

  1628	\begin{equation}
  1629	\label{eq:qld-constructing-the-paulis-helper0}

  1633	\[
  1634	\sum_g (\hat{S}^W_g)_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\hat{M}^{(\Point, W), u}_{g(u)})_{\bob \alice''} \approx_{\delta_S} \Id.

  1636	
  1637	We now prove \Cref{eq:qld-sg-cons2}. \Cref{eq:qld-constructing-the-paulis-helper0} and \Cref{fact:agreement} shows that
  1638	\[ (\hat{S}^W_{[g(u)=a]})_{\alice \alice'} \approx_{\delta_S} (\hat{M}^{(\Point, W), u}_{a})_{\bob \alice''}\]
  1639	where the answer summation is over $a \in \F_q$. Left-multiplying this expression by $(\hat{S}^W_{[g(u)=a]})_{\alice \alice'}$ and using \Cref{fact:add-a-proj} we get
  1640	\begin{align*}

  1645	\begin{align}

  1648		= & \E_u \sum_a \left \| (\hat{M}^{(\Point, W), u}_{a})_{\alice \alice'} - (\hat{M}^{(\Point, W), u}_{a})_{\bob \alice''} \ket{\hat{\psi}} \right \|^2 \\

  1666	 The next lemma shows that we can construct local unitaries $V_A,V_B$ from the measurements $\hat{S}$  such that the shared state $\ket{\hat{\psi}}$ is close to $\ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}$ for some state $\ket{\aux}$, and the observables $\tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u})$ are mapped to Pauli observables $\tau^W(e_j \tilde{u})$ acting on $\ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}$.   1669	\begin{lemma}
  1670	\label{lem:qld-unitary}
  1671	There exists a function $\delta_\qld(\eps,m,d,q) = O(\delta_S^{1/4} + md/q)$ (where $\delta_S$ is defined in \Cref{lem:qld-4-7}) and unitaries $V_\alice$ acting on registers $\alice \alice' \alice''$ and $V_\bob$ acting on $\bob \bob' \bob''$ such that 
  1672	\begin{enumerate}
  1673		\item There exists a state $\ket{\aux}$ on registers $\alice \alice' \bob \bob'$ such that
  1674		\[
  1675			\left \| V_\alice \otimes V_\bob \ket{\hat{\psi}}_{\alice \alice' \alice'' \bob \bob' \bob''} - \ket{\aux}_{\alice \alice' \bob \bob'} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}_{\alice'' \bob''} \right \|^2 \leq \delta_\qld.
  1676		\]
  1677		
  1678		\item For all $W \in \{X,Z\}, h \in \F_q^\nqubits$
  1679		\begin{align*}
  1680			V_\alice \, \Big(M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \Big)_{\alice} \, V_\alice^\dagger &\approx_{\delta_\qld} \Id_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\tau^W_h)_{\alice''} \\
  1681			 V_\bob \, \Big(M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h  \Big)_{\bob}\, V_\bob^\dagger &\approx_{\delta_\qld} \Id_{\bob \bob'} \otimes (\tau^W_h)_{\bob''}
  1682		\end{align*}
  1683		where the $\approx$ statements hold with respect to the state $\ket{\aux}_{\alice \alice' \bob \bob'} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}_{\alice'' \bob''}$. 
  1684	\end{enumerate}
  1685	\end{lemma}
  1686	
  1687	\begin{proof}
  1688	
  1689	Define the linear map
  1690	\[
  1691		V_\alice = \sum_{g_X,g_Z} (\hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z})_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)))_{\alice ''}\;,
  1692	\]
  1693	where the $\tau^X(\cdot),\tau^Z(\cdot)$ act on $(\C^q)^{\otimes \nqubits}$. (Also note that the argument of $\tau^X$ is $\coded(g_Z)$ and the argument of $\tau^Z$ is $\coded(g_X)$.) We verify the unitarity of $V_\alice$:
  1694	\begin{align*}
  1695		V_\alice V_\alice^\dagger &= \sum_{g_X,g_Z} (\hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z})_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)) \tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) )_{\alice ''} \\
  1696		&= \sum_{g_X,g_Z} (\hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z})_{\alice \alice'} \otimes \Id_{\alice ''} \\
  1697		&= \Id_{\alice \alice' \alice''}
  1698	\end{align*}
  1699	where in the first line we used that the measurement $\{ \hat{S}_{g_\xpt,g_\zpt} \}$  is projective and in the second line we used that the $\tau^Z$ and $\tau^X$ observables are self-inverse. The unitary $V_\bob$ is defined analogously.
  1700	
  1701	Let $\{e_j\}_{j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}}$ denote the self-dual basis for $\F_q$ over $\F_2$ specified in \Cref{sec:subfields}, and let $\tilde{W}^j$ be the observables introduced in~\eqref{eq:def-tildewj}. Conjugating the observable $\tilde{W}^j$ acting on the registers $\alice \alice' \alice''$ by the unitary $V_\alice$ we get
  1702	\begin{align*}
  1703		&V_\alice \, \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \, V_\alice^\dagger \\
  1704	  =& \sum_{g_X, g_Z} (-1)^{\tr( e_j(\coded(g_W) \cdot \tilde{u}))} \Big( \hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}  \Big)_{\alice \alice'} \otimes \Big ( \tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)) \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \\
  1705	  &\hspace{24em}\tau^Z(\coded(g_X))^\dagger \tau^X(\coded(g_Z))^\dagger \Big)_{\alice ''} \\
  1706		 =& \sum_{g_X, g_Z} \Big( \hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}  \Big)_{\alice \alice'} \otimes \Big ( \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \Big)_{\alice ''} \\
  1707		 =& \Id_{\alice \alice'} \otimes \Big( \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \Big)_{\alice ''}\;,
  1708	\end{align*}
  1709	where in the third line we used the (anti-)commutation relation
  1710	\[
  1711		\tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)) \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) = (-1)^{\tr( e_j(\coded(g_W) \cdot \tilde{u}))} \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)) \;.
  1712	\]
  1713	An entirely analogous calculation shows that $V_\bob \, \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \, V_\bob^\dagger = \Id_{\bob \bob'} \otimes \Big( \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \Big)_{\bob ''}$.
  1714	
  1715	Next, from the self-consistency property of the observables $\tilde{W}^j$ specified in \Cref{lem:qld-construct-the-paulis} we get that for $W \in \{X,Z\}$,
  1716	\[
  1717		\E_{j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}} \E_{\tilde{u} \in \F_q^\nqubits} \bra{\hat{\psi}} \left ( \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \otimes \Id - \Id \otimes \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \right)^\dagger \left ( \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \otimes \Id - \Id \otimes \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \right) \ket{\hat{\psi}} \leq \delta_S\;,
  1718	\]
  1719	which, since $\tilde{W}^j$ is Hermitian, is equivalent to
  1720	\begin{equation}
  1721	\label{eq:qld-unitary-1}
  1722	\E_{j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}} \E_{\tilde{u} \in \F_q^\nqubits} \bra{\hat{\psi}} \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \otimes \tilde{W}^j(\tilde{u}) \ket{\hat{\psi}} \geq 1 - \delta_S/2\;.
  1723	\end{equation}
  1724	Let $\ket{\vartheta} = V_\alice \otimes V_\bob \ket{\hat{\psi}}$, and for $W \in \{X,Z\}$ define the operator
  1725	\begin{align*}
  1726		H_W &= \E_{j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}} \E_{\tilde{u} \in \F_q^\nqubits} \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \otimes \tau^W(e_j \tilde{u}) \\
  1727			&= \E_{j \in \{1,\ldots,t\}} \Big ( \E_{s \in \F_q} \tau^W(e_j s) \otimes \tau^W(e_j s) \Big)^{\otimes \nqubits} \\
  1728			&= \Big ( \E_{s \in \F_q} \tau^W(s) \otimes \tau^W(s) \Big)^{\otimes \nqubits}
  1729	\end{align*}
  1730	where in the second line we used that for all $\tilde{u} \in \F_q^\nqubits$, $\tau^W(\tilde{u}) = \bigotimes_{i = 1}^\nqubits \tau^W(\tilde{u}_i)$ with $\tau^W(\tilde{u}_i)$ being the generalized Pauli $W$ observable acting on the $i$-th qudit. In the third line, we used the fact that for every fixed $j$, we have $\E_{s \in \F_q} \tau^W(e_j s) \otimes \tau^W(e_j s) = \E_{s \in \F_q} \tau^W(s) \otimes \tau^W(s)$. \Cref{eq:qld-unitary-1} is then equivalent to 
  1731	\[
  1732		\bra{\vartheta} H_W \ket{\vartheta} \geq 1 - \delta_S/2\;,
  1733	\]
  1734	for $W \in \{X,Z\}$. 
  1735	
  1736	Observe that
  1737	\begin{align*}
  1738		\E_{s,s'} \tau^X(s) \tau^Z(s') \otimes \tau^X(s) \tau^Z(s') &= \E_{s,s'} \sum_{a,b \in \F_q} (-1)^{\tr(as')} \ketbra{a+s}{a} \otimes (-1)^{\tr(bs')} \ketbra{b+s}{b} \\
  1739		&= \E_{s} \sum_{a\in \F_q} \ketbra{a+s}{a} \otimes \ketbra{a+s}{a} \\
  1740		&= \proj{\EPR_q}
  1741	\end{align*}
  1742	where to go from the first to the second line we used \Cref{lem:cancellation}. This implies that $H_X H_Z = \Big ( \E_{s,s' \in \F_q} \tau^X(s)\tau^Z(s') \otimes \tau^X(s)\tau^Z(s') \Big)^{\otimes \nqubits} = \ketbra{\EPR_q}{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}$.
  1743	By the triangle inequality, we have
  1744	\[
  1745		\left \| H_X \ket{\vartheta} - H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \right\| \leq \left \| \ket{\vartheta} - H_X \ket{\vartheta} \right\| + \left \| \ket{\vartheta} - H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \right\|\;.
  1746	\]
  1747	Note that for $W \in \{X,Z\}$,
  1748	\[
  1749		\left \| \ket{\vartheta} - H_W \ket{\vartheta} \right\|^2 = 1 - 2\bra{\vartheta} H_W \ket{\vartheta} + \bra{\vartheta} H_W^2 \ket{\vartheta} \leq 2 - 2\bra{\vartheta} H_W \ket{\vartheta} \leq \delta_S\;,
  1750	\]
  1751	where in the inequality we used that $H_W \leq \Id$. Furthermore,
  1752	\begin{align*}
  1753		\bra{\vartheta} H_W^2 \ket{\vartheta} &=\| H_W \ket{\vartheta} \|^2\\
  1754		 &= \| \ket{\vartheta} + (H_W - \Id) \ket{\vartheta} \|^2 \\
  1755		 &\geq (\|\ket{\vartheta}\| - \| (H_W - \Id) \ket{\vartheta} \|)^2 \\
  1756		 &\geq (1 - \delta_S)^2 \\
  1757		 &\geq 1 - 2\delta_S\;. 
  1758	\end{align*}
  1759	Therefore 
  1760	\begin{align*}
  1761	2\sqrt{\delta_S} &\geq \left \| H_X \ket{\vartheta} - H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \right\|^2  \\
  1762	&= \bra{\vartheta} H_X^2 \ket{\vartheta} + \bra{\vartheta} H_Z^2 \ket{\vartheta} - 2\bra{\vartheta} H_X H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \\
  1763	&\geq 2 - 4\delta_S - 2\bra{\vartheta} H_X H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \;,
  1764	\end{align*}
  1765	which implies that 
  1766	\[
  1767		\bra{\vartheta} (\Id_{\alice \alice' \bob \bob'} \otimes (\proj{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits})_{\alice'' \bob''}) \ket{\vartheta} \geq 1 - 2\delta_S - \sqrt{\delta_S} \;.
  1768	\]
  1769	Define the unnormalized state $\ket{\aux_0}$ on the registers $\alice \alice' \bob \bob'$ as
  1770	\[
  1771		\ket{\aux_0}_{\alice \alice' \bob \bob'} = (\bra{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits})_{\alice'' \bob''} \cdot \ket{\vartheta}_{\alice \alice' \alice'' \bob \bob' \bob''}
  1772	\]
  1773	and define the normalized state $\ket{\aux} = \frac{1}{\| \, \ket{\aux_0} \, \|} \ket{\aux_0}$. 
  1774	The inner product between $\ket{\vartheta}$ and $\ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}$ can thus be evaluated as
  1775	\begin{align*}
  1776		\bra{\vartheta} (\ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}) &= \frac{1}{\| \, \ket{\aux_0} \, \|} \cdot \bra{\vartheta} (\ket{\aux_0} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}) \\
  1777		&= \frac{1}{\| \, \ket{\aux_0} \, \|} \cdot \bra{\vartheta} (\Id_{\alice \alice' \bob \bob'} \otimes (\proj{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits})_{\alice'' \bob''}) \ket{\vartheta} \\
  1778		&= \frac{1}{\| \, \ket{\aux_0} \, \|} \cdot \| \, \ket{\aux_0} \, \|^2 \\
  1779		&= \| \, \ket{\aux_0} \, \| \\
  1780		&\geq \sqrt{1 - 2\delta_S - \sqrt{\delta_S}} \\
  1781		&\geq 1 - O(\sqrt{\delta_S})\;.
  1782	\end{align*}
  1783	This implies $\| \ket{\vartheta} - \ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits} \|^2 \leq O(\sqrt{\delta_S})$, which establishes the first item of the lemma.
  1784	
  1785	We now establish the second item of the lemma. In what follows, all $\simeq$ and $\approx$ statements hold with respect to the state $\ket{\hat{\psi}}$. From \Cref{lem:qld-win-implications} we have the following implications: for all $W \in \{X,Z\}$ and on average over $u \in \F_q^m$,
  1786		\begin{align}
  1787		\label{eq:qld-unitary-2}
  1788		M^{(\Pauli,W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \otimes \Id_{\bob \bob' \bob''} &\simeq_\eps \Id_{\alice \alice' \alice''} \otimes M^{(\Point,W),u}_a\;, \\
  1789		\label{eq:qld-unitary-3}
  1790		\Id_{\alice \alice' \alice''} \otimes M^{(\Point,W),u}_a &\simeq_\eps  M^{(\Point,W),u}_a \otimes \Id_{\bob \bob' \bob''}\;,
  1791		\end{align}
  1792		where $M^{(\Pauli,W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} = \sum_{h : g_h(u) = a} M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h$. 
  1793	From \Cref{lem:qld-construct-the-paulis} we get that
  1794		\begin{equation}
  1795		\label{eq:qld-unitary-4}
  1796			M^{(\Point,W),u}_a \otimes \Id_{\bob \bob' \bob''} \simeq_{\delta_S} \Id_{\alice \alice' \alice''}  \otimes \tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a\;.
  1797		\end{equation}
  1798	Using \Cref{fact:triangle-for-simeq} with Equations \eqref{eq:qld-unitary-2}, \eqref{eq:qld-unitary-3}, and \eqref{eq:qld-unitary-4}, we get 
  1799		\begin{equation}
  1800			\label{eq:qld-unitary-5}
  1801			M^{(\Pauli,W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \otimes \Id_{\bob \bob' \bob''} \simeq_{\sqrt{\delta_S}} \Id_{\alice \alice' \alice''}  \otimes \tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a\;,
  1802		\end{equation}
  1803		where we used that $\delta_S \geq \eps$. 
  1804		
  1805		Next, we have for all $u \in \F_q^m$ 
  1806		\begin{align}
  1807			&V_\bob \, \tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a \, V_\bob^\dagger \notag \\
  1808			= &\sum_{g_X, g_Z} \Big( \hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}  \Big)_{\bob \bob'} \otimes \Big ( \tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)) \tau^W_{g_W(u) - a}(\ind_m(u))    \tau^Z(\coded(g_X))^\dagger \tau^X(\coded(g_Z))^\dagger \Big)_{\bob ''} \notag \\
  1809			= &\sum_{g_X, g_Z} \Big( \hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}  \Big)_{\bob \bob'} \otimes \sum_{h : g_h(u) = g_W(u) - a} \Big ( \tau^X(\coded(g_Z)) \tau^Z(\coded(g_X)) \tau^W_h   \tau^Z(\coded(g_X))^\dagger \tau^X(\coded(g_Z))^\dagger \Big)_{\bob ''} \notag \\
  1810			= &\sum_{g_X, g_Z} \Big( \hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}  \Big)_{\bob \bob'} \otimes \sum_{h : g_h(u) = g_W(u) - a} \Big ( \tau^W_{h + \coded(g_W)}   \Big)_{\bob ''} \notag \\
  1811		= &\sum_{g_X, g_Z} \Big( \hat{S}_{g_X,g_Z}  \Big)_{\bob \bob'} \otimes \sum_{h : g_h(u) = a} \Big ( \tau^W_{h}   \Big)_{\bob ''} \notag \\
  1812	= &\Id_{\bob \bob'} \otimes (\tau^W_{[g_h(u)=a]})_{\bob''}\;,		\label{eq:qld-unitary-6}
  1813		\end{align}
  1814		where in the second line we expanded out the definitions of $V_\bob$ and $\tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a$ (defined in \cref{eq:tilde_M}); in the third line we expanded out the definition of $\tau^W_{g_W(u) - a}(\ind_m(u))$ (defined in \cref{eq:def-tauwu}) and used the fact that for all $h \in \F_q^M$, the inner product $h \cdot \ind_m(u)$ is equal to $g_h(u)$; in the fourth line we used the identities
  1815		\[
  1816			\tau^X(s) \tau^Z_h \tau^X(s)^\dagger = \tau^Z_{h + s} \qquad \text{and} \qquad \tau^Z(s) \tau^X_h \tau^Z(s)^\dagger = \tau^X_{h + s}~;
  1817		\]
  1818		and in the fifth line is due to the following short calculation: for all fixed $g_W$ we have
  1819		\begin{align*}
  1820			\sum_{h : g_h(u) = g_W(u) - a}  \tau^W_{h + \coded(g_W)} = \sum_{h: g_W(u) - g_h(u) = a} \tau^W_{h + \coded(g_W)} = \sum_{h: g_W(u) + g_h(u) = a} \tau^W_{h + \coded(g_W)} = \sum_{h': g_{h'}(u) = a} \tau^W_{h'}~.
  1821		\end{align*}
  1822		The second equality from the fact that $\F_q$ is a field of characteristic $2$ (so subtraction is the same as addition), and the third equality follows from the fact that letting $h' = h + \coded(g_W)$, we have $g_{h'} = g_h + g_W$ (in other words, the low-degree encoding $h \mapsto g_h$ is linear in $h$). 
  1823		
  1824		
  1825	
  1826	
  1827	Let $\ket{\Delta} = \ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}$. We show that $V_\alice \, \Big(M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \Big)_{\alice} \, V_\alice^\dagger \approx_{\delta_\qld} \Id_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\tau^W_h)_{\alice''}$ (the argument for the operators acting on registers $\bob \bob' \bob''$ proceeds identically). 
  1828		\begin{align}
  1829			&\sum_h \bra{\Delta} \left ( V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger - (\tau^W_h)_{\alice''}  \right)^\dagger \left ( V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger - (\tau^W_h)_{\alice''} \right) \ket{\Delta} \notag \\
  1830			&= 2 - 2 \Re \, \sum_h \bra{\Delta} V_\alice\, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger  \, (\tau^W_h)_{\alice''} \ket{\Delta} \notag \\
  1831			&= 2 - 2 \, \sum_h \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger  \, \otimes (\tau^W_h)_{\bob''} \ket{\Delta} \label{eq:qld-unitary-7}
  1832	\end{align}
  1833		where in the last line we used that $(\tau^W_h)_{\alice''} \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits} = (\tau^W_h)_{\bob''} \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}$.
  1834		We now claim that
  1835		\begin{align}
  1836		&  \, \sum_h \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger  \, \otimes (\tau^W_h)_{\bob''} \ket{\Delta}  \notag \\
  1837		&\approx_{md/q}  \E_u \sum_{\substack{h, h' : \\ g_h(u) = g_{h'}(u)}} \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger  \, \otimes (\tau^W_{h'})_{\bob''} \ket{\Delta} \label{eq:qld-unitary-8} \\
  1838		&=  \E_u \sum_{a \in \F_q} \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \, V_\alice^\dagger \, \otimes (\tau^W_{[g_h(u)=a]})_{\bob''} \ket{\Delta} \notag \\
  1839		&=  \E_u \sum_{a \in \F_q} \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \, V_\alice^\dagger \, \otimes V_\bob  \, \tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a \, V_\bob^\dagger \ket{\Delta} \label{eq:qld-unitary-9}
  1840		\end{align}
  1841		where the equality in \Cref{eq:qld-unitary-9} follows from the identity in \Cref{eq:qld-unitary-6}, and the approximation in \Cref{eq:qld-unitary-8} follows from the following calculation:
  1842		\begin{align*}
  1843			& \E_u \sum_{\substack{h \neq h' : \\ g_h(u) = g_{h'}(u)}} \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger  \, \otimes (\tau^W_{h'})_{\bob''} \ket{\Delta}  \\
  1844			&= \sum_{h \neq h'} \left( \E_u \mathbf{1}[g_h(u) = g_{h'}(u)] \right) \bra{\Delta} V_\alice \, M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \, V_\alice^\dagger  \, \otimes (\tau^W_{h'})_{\bob''} \ket{\Delta} \\
  1845			&\leq \frac{md}{q}\;.
  1846		\end{align*}
  1847		In the last line we used that for for distinct $h \neq h'$, the polynomials $g_h \neq g_{h'}$ and thus by the Schwartz-Zippel lemma can only agree on at most $md/q$ fraction of points $u \in \F_q^m$. 
  1848		
  1849		Continuing from \Cref{eq:qld-unitary-9}, we use the first item of the Lemma which shows that $\| \ket{\Delta} - \ket{\vartheta} \|^2 \leq O(\sqrt{\delta_S})$ and equivalently $\| V_\alice^\dagger \otimes V_\bob^\dagger \ket{\Delta} - \ket{\hat{\psi}} \|^2 \leq O(\sqrt{\delta_S})$, so 
  1850		\begin{align*}
  1851			\text{\cref{eq:qld-unitary-9}} &\approx_{O(\delta_S^{1/4})} \E_u \sum_{a \in \F_q} \bra{\hat{\psi}} M^{(\Pauli,W)}_{[g_h(u)=a]} \otimes \tilde{M}^{W,\ind_m(u)}_a \ket{\hat{\psi}} \\
  1852			&\geq 1 - O(\delta_S^{1/2})\;,
  1853		\end{align*}
  1854	        where the last line comes from \eqref{eq:qld-unitary-5}.
  1855		Together with \Cref{eq:qld-unitary-7}, 
  1856		\[
  1857		\text{\cref{eq:qld-unitary-7}} \leq O(\delta_S^{1/4} + md/q)\;.	
  1858		\]
  1859		This concludes the proof of the second item of the lemma.
  1860	\end{proof}

  1862	We now prove \Cref{thm:pauli-appendix}. 
  1863	\begin{proof}[Proof of \Cref{thm:pauli-appendix}]
  1864		Let $\strategy = (\psi,M)$ be a projective strategy for $\game^\pauli_\qldparams$ that succeeds with probability at least $1 - \eps$, where $\ket{\psi}$ is a bipartite state on registers $\alice \bob$. As mentioned at the beginning of \Cref{sec:commutation}, we assume that the state $\ket{\psi}$ is padded with sufficiently many ancilla $\ket{0}$ qubits. Let $\phi_\alice$ be the following isometry mapping the register $\alice$ to the registers $\alice \alice' \alice''$ where $\alice'$ and $\alice''$ are isomorphic to $(\C^q)^{\otimes \nqubits}$:
  1865		\[
  1866			\phi_\alice: \ket{\theta}_\alice \mapsto V_\alice (\ket{\theta}_\alice \otimes (\ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits})_{\alice' \alice''})
  1867		\]
  1868		where $V_\alice$ is the unitary acting on $\alice \alice' \alice''$ from \Cref{lem:qld-unitary}. Define the isometry $\phi_\bob$ analogously. \Cref{lem:qld-unitary} then implies that there exists a state $\ket{\aux}$ on registers $\alice \alice' \bob \bob'$ such that
  1869		\[
  1870			\left \| \phi_\alice \otimes \phi_\bob \ket{\psi} - \ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits} \right \|^2 \leq \delta_\qld
  1871		\]
  1872		and for $W \in \{X,Z\}$,
  1873		\[
  1874			\phi_\alice \, (M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h)_\alice \, \phi_\alice^\dagger \approx_{\delta_\qld} (\tau^W_h)_{\alice''} \qquad \text{and} \qquad \phi_\bob \, (M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h)_\bob \, \phi_\bob^\dagger \approx_{\delta_\qld} (\tau^W_h)_{\bob''}
  1875		\]
  1876		where the $\approx$ statement holds with respect to the state $\ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}$. This shows that $\game^\pauli_\qldparams$ is a self-test for the strategy $\strategy^\pauli$ with robustness $\delta_\qld(\eps,m,d,q)$. We conclude the proof by making the identification of registers $\alice \alice'$ with $\alice'$ and $\bob \bob'$ with $\bob'$ to be consistent with the statement of \Cref{thm:pauli-appendix}. We also note that, when unpacking the dependence on parameters $\eps, m, d, q$, the function $\delta_\qld(\eps,m,d,q) = O(\delta_S^{1/4} + md/q)$ has the form $a(md)^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$ for some universal constants $a > 1, 0 < b < 1$, as desired.
  1877	\end{proof}

     3	/-!
     4	# Extraction foundations
     5	
     6	This module supplies the witness-independent register bookkeeping used to pull
     7	the Pauli measurements apart. It retains the distinct local spaces of a
     8	heterogeneous strategy, coarse-grains the generalized Pauli projectors by a
     9	dot product, and records the state and error expressions needed by the later
    10	extraction witness.
    11	
    12	The binary phases use the existing `phaseSign`; the fixed field basis remains
    13	the basis stored in `P.model` and is not re-quantified here.
    14	
    15	## References
    16	
    17	The Pauli dot-product projectors formalize `def:tau-dot-product-projector` in
    18	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:46-53`, from
    19	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1426-1429`.
    20	The register and state helpers support `def:tilde-m-measurement`,
    21	`def:v-swap-unitary`, and `lem:qld-unitary`, from paper lines 1429-1435 and
    22	1666-1713 and blueprint lines 55-62 and 203-260.
    23	-/
    24	
    25	open scoped BigOperators Matrix
    26	
    27	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    28	
    29	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    30	
    31	noncomputable section
    32	
    33	/-! ## Heterogeneous extraction registers -/
    34	
    35	/-- One player's registers after adjoining the two generalized-Pauli
    36	registers: `AA'A''` or `BB'B''`. This identifies the register order and spaces for
    37	paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1429-1435,1687-1713` and
    38	blueprint `ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:55-62,203-230`. -/
    39	abbrev ExtractionBlock (P : AdmissibleParams) (ι : Type*) :=
    40	  (ι × PauliRegister P) × PauliRegister P
    41	
    42	/-- The two heterogeneous extraction blocks in the order
    43	`AA'A'' | BB'B''`. This is the block presentation of the existing `SixReg`
    44	space used in `lem:qld-unitary`, blueprint
    45	`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:245-260`, paper
    46	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1685`. -/
    47	abbrev ExtractionRegisters (P : AdmissibleParams) (ιA ιB : Type*) :=
    48	  ExtractionBlock P ιA × ExtractionBlock P ιB
    49	
    50	/-- The auxiliary registers `AA'BB'` occurring before the extracted EPR
    51	factor in `lem:qld-unitary`, blueprint `ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:245-260`,
    52	paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1685`. -/
    53	abbrev ExtractionAuxRegisters (P : AdmissibleParams) (ιA ιB : Type*) :=
    54	  (ιA × PauliRegister P) × (ιB × PauliRegister P)
    55	
    56	/-- Reassociate the landed six-register order with the two extraction blocks.
    57	This equivalence identifies the register order in paper
    58	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1429-1435,1687-1713`. -/
    59	def sixRegExtractionEquiv (P : AdmissibleParams) (ιA ιB : Type*) :
    60	    SixReg P ιA ιB ≃ ExtractionRegisters P ιA ιB where
    61	  toFun p := (((p.1.1, p.1.2.1), p.1.2.2),
    62	    ((p.2.1, p.2.2.1), p.2.2.2))
    63	  invFun p := ((p.1.1.1, (p.1.1.2, p.1.2)),
    64	    (p.2.1.1, (p.2.1.2, p.2.2)))
    65	  left_inv p := by cases p; rfl
    66	  right_inv p := by cases p; rfl
    67	
    68	/-- Shuffle `AA'BB' | A''B''` into the landed six-register order. This is
    69	Lean-only bookkeeping for the ideal state in `lem:qld-unitary`, blueprint
    70	`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:245-260`, paper
    71	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1685`. -/
    72	def extractionIdealShuffle (P : AdmissibleParams) (ιA ιB : Type*) :
    73	    (ExtractionAuxRegisters P ιA ιB ×
    74	      (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P)) ≃ SixReg P ιA ιB where
    75	  toFun p := ((p.1.1.1, (p.1.1.2, p.2.1)),
    76	    (p.1.2.1, (p.1.2.2, p.2.2)))
    77	  invFun p := (((p.1.1, p.1.2.1), (p.2.1, p.2.2.1)),
    78	    (p.1.2.2, p.2.2.2))
    79	  left_inv p := by cases p; rfl
    80	  right_inv p := by cases p; rfl

    82	namespace ProjectiveSetting
    83	
    84	variable {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ}
    85	
    86	/-- Place an operator on one complete extraction block, with the identity on
    87	the other player's block. This is the heterogeneous Lean realization of the
    88	side-qualified operators in paper
    89	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1429-1435,1687-1713`. -/
    90	noncomputable def placeSide (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
    91	    (O : Op (ExtractionBlock P (S.LocalSpace side))) :
    92	    Op (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) := by
    93	  cases side with
    94	  | alice =>
    95	      exact reindexOp
    96	        (sixRegExtractionEquiv P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
    97	        (heteroKron O 1)
    98	  | bob =>
    99	      exact reindexOp
   100	        (sixRegExtractionEquiv P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
   101	        (heteroKron 1 O)
   102	
   103	/-- Lift an operator on a player's original strategy register to that player's
   104	full extraction block. This is Lean-only support for the raw Pauli and point
   105	measurements in `lem:qld-construct-the-paulis` and `lem:qld-unitary`, blueprint
   106	`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:105-124,245-260`. -/
   107	noncomputable def onPlayer (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
   108	    (O : Op (S.LocalSpace side)) :
   109	    Op (ExtractionBlock P (S.LocalSpace side)) :=
   110	  heteroKron (heteroKron O 1) 1
   111	
   112	/-- Place an operator on the original strategy register of the selected
   113	player. This helper uses the landed `ProjectiveSetting.place` API and is
   114	Lean-only support for the player-side conclusions of `lem:qld-unitary`,
   115	blueprint `ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:245-260`. -/
   116	noncomputable def placePlayer (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
   117	    (O : Op (S.LocalSpace side)) :
   118	    Op (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) := by
   119	  cases side with
   120	  | alice => exact S.place .AA' (heteroKron O 1)
   121	  | bob => exact S.place .BB' (heteroKron O 1)
   122	
   123	/-- Place an operator on the selected extracted register `A''` or `B''`.
   124	The unused strategy register in the landed crossed placement is assigned the
   125	identity. This is Lean-only support for the ideal Pauli operators in
   126	`lem:qld-unitary`, blueprint `ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:245-260`, paper
   127	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1685`. -/
   128	noncomputable def placeExtractedRegister (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   129	    (side : PlayerSide) (O : Op (PauliRegister P)) :
   130	    Op (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) := by
   131	  cases side with
   132	  | alice =>
   133	      exact S.place .BA'' (heteroKron (1 : Op S.toStrategy.ιB) O)
   134	  | bob =>
   135	      exact S.place .AB'' (heteroKron (1 : Op S.toStrategy.ιA) O)
   136	
   137	/-- Place a pair of block operators simultaneously on `AA'A''` and
   138	`BB'B''`. This is Lean-only support for the transformed state in
   139	`lem:qld-unitary`, blueprint `ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:245-260`, paper
   140	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1685`. -/
   141	noncomputable def placeBoth (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   142	    (VA : Op (ExtractionBlock P S.toStrategy.ιA))
   143	    (VB : Op (ExtractionBlock P S.toStrategy.ιB)) :
   144	    Op (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) :=
   145	  reindexOp (sixRegExtractionEquiv P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
   146	    (heteroKron VA VB)
   147	
   148	/-- Apply one operator to each heterogeneous extraction block. This is the
   149	witness-independent state transformation used for `V_A tensor V_B` in
   150	`lem:qld-unitary`, blueprint `ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:245-260`, paper
   151	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1685`. -/
   152	noncomputable def applyBoth (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   153	    (VA : Op (ExtractionBlock P S.toStrategy.ιA))
   154	    (VB : Op (ExtractionBlock P S.toStrategy.ιB))
   155	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ
   156	      (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)) :
   157	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) :=
   158	  applyOperatorToState (S.placeBoth VA VB) ψ
   159	
   160	/-- The state `aux tensor EPR_q^{tensor M}` in the landed six-register order.
   161	This is the ideal state in Item 1 of `lem:qld-unitary`, blueprint
   162	`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:245-260`, paper
   163	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1666-1685`. -/
   164	noncomputable def idealExpState (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   165	    (aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ
   166	      (ExtractionAuxRegisters P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)) :
   167	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) := by
   168	  classical
   169	  exact
   170	    reindexState (extractionIdealShuffle P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
   171	      (vecTensor aux (eprState (PauliRegister P)))
   172	
   173	end ProjectiveSetting

   175	/-! ## Coarse-grained Pauli projectors -/
   176	
   177	/-- Coarse-grain a finite operator family along a map of outcomes. This is the
   178	operator-valued sum corresponding to `Measurement.postprocess`, used by
   179	`def:tau-dot-product-projector`, blueprint
   180	`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:46-53`. -/
   181	noncomputable def bracketOp {α β ι : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq β]
   182	    (N : α → Op ι) (f : α → β) (b : β) : Op ι :=
   183	  ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), N a
   184	
   185	/-- The effect of a postprocessed measurement is the corresponding
   186	coarse-grained operator sum. This equality is used by `def:bracket` and
   187	`def:tau-dot-product-projector`, blueprint
   188	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:8-26` and `ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:46-53`. -/
   189	theorem postprocess_effect_eq_bracketOp {α β ι : Type*}
   190	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β]
   191	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (M : Measurement α ι) (f : α → β) (b : β) :
   192	    (M.postprocess f).effect b = bracketOp M.effect f b :=

   201	    (u : PauliRegister P) (a : PauliScalar P) : Op (PauliRegister P) :=

   229	
   230	/-- Conjugation of an operator by a square matrix. This is Lean-only notation
   231	for the exact conjugation equations in `lem:v-swap-conjugation`, blueprint

323	\begin{remark}[Two steps in the source proof of the extraction lemma]\label{rem:qld-unitary-triangle-slip}
   324		In the source proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-unitary}, the triangle inequality gives $\| H_X \ket{\vartheta} - H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \| \leq \| (\Id - H_X)\ket{\vartheta} \| + \| (\Id - H_Z)\ket{\vartheta} \| \leq 2\sqrt{\delta_P}$, so that $\| H_X \ket{\vartheta} - H_Z \ket{\vartheta} \|^2 \leq 4\delta_P$; the source instead asserts the bound $2\sqrt{\delta_P}$ for the \emph{squared} norm, which holds only when $\sqrt{\delta_P} \leq 1/2$, and consequently carries the term $\sqrt{\delta_P}$ into an overlap bound of $1 - 2\delta_P - \sqrt{\delta_P}$. The proof above uses the corrected bound $4\delta_P$, which gives the overlap bound $1 - 4\delta_P$ and leaves the final bound $\delta_{\mathrm{qld}} = O(\delta_P^{1/4} + md/q)$ unchanged. The source proof also normalizes the vector $(\bra{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M})_{\mathrm{A}''\mathrm{B}''} \ket{\vartheta}$ without ensuring that it is nonzero; the case distinction on $\delta_P$ in the proof above supplies this, the conclusions of the lemma being trivial when $\delta_P$ exceeds a universal constant.
   325	\end{remark}
   326	
   327	\section{Proof of the soundness of the Pauli basis test}
   328	
   329	We can now prove the soundness theorem for the Pauli basis test, stated as Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli} in Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-test}.
   330	
   331	\begin{proof}
   332		\proves{thm:pauli}
   333		\uses{lem:qld-unitary, lem:pauli-completeness, thm:naimark, lem:projective-strategy-setup, def:expanded-state, def:EPR, def:povm-distance}
   334		Let $(\ket{\psi},M)$ be a strategy for $\mathfrak{G}^{\mathrm{Pauli}}_{(q,m,d)}$ that succeeds with probability at least $1 - \eps$, where $\ket{\psi}$ is a bipartite state on registers $\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathrm{B}$. By Naimark's theorem (Theorem~\ref{thm:naimark}, as formulated in~\cite[Theorem 5.1]{Ji2020LowIndividualDegree}), at the cost of extending $\ket{\psi}$ by sufficiently many ancilla qubits initialized in the state $\ket{0}$, we may assume that the strategy is projective and that the state is padded as in the conventions of Lemma~\ref{lem:projective-strategy-setup} and the convention following it. Let $V_{\mathrm{A}}$ be the unitary acting on registers $\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''$ given by Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-unitary}, and let $\phi_{\mathrm{A}}$ be the isometry mapping register $\mathrm{A}$ to registers $\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''$, where $\mathrm{A}'$ and $\mathrm{A}''$ are isomorphic to $(\C^q)^{\ot M}$, defined by
   335		\[
   336			\phi_{\mathrm{A}}\colon \ket{\theta}_{\mathrm{A}} \mapsto V_{\mathrm{A}} \bigl(\ket{\theta}_{\mathrm{A}} \ot (\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M})_{\mathrm{A}' \mathrm{A}''}\bigr)\;;
   337		\]
   338		define $\phi_{\mathrm{B}}$ analogously.
   339		% Reliance disclosure added: the proof chain of thm:pauli passes through
   340		% lem:qld-4-7, whose source proof (lines 1277--1413 of
   341		% 14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex) instantiates the classical low
   342		% individual degree test at dimension 2m+2 without a divisibility
   343		% hypothesis; the sentence below records the resulting outstanding
   344		% obligation.
   345		This invocation is where the analysis of the classical low individual degree test enters: Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-unitary} rests on the polynomial-pair measurement of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-7}, whose proof instantiates the classical test in $2m+2$ variables and at present does so only when $2m+2$ divides $q$ --- a divisibility that fails for every admissible tuple with $m \geq 2$. Three further steps of that same chain are likewise unproved. The classical soundness statement invoked there, Theorem~\ref{lem:ld-soundness}, is imported from Theorem~4.7 of~\cite{Ji2021Quantum} through an identification of the game $\mathfrak{G}^{\mathrm{ld}}_{(q,m,d,1)}$ with the two-prover tensor-code test for $\code^{\ot m}$, and neither that game correspondence nor the bound on the auxiliary parameter of Theorem~4.7 under which the stated error function $\delta_{\mathrm{ld}}$ is obtained has been established; both, with the divisibility obstruction, are documented in \cite{gap:qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility}. Furthermore, the combined-lines consistency of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-13}, which Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-7} consumes, is established here only with the error $m \cdot \poly(\eps, md/q)$, the error form $\poly(m^2 \eps, md/q)$ carried in its statement remaining unproved (see \cite{gap:qpbt_combined-lines-error-term}). The present proof is therefore complete only modulo these four obligations. Since the expanded state $\ket{\hat\psi}$ of Definition~\ref{def:expanded-state} is exactly $\ket{\psi}$ with the halves of $M$ pairs $\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}$ appended locally in registers $\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''$ and $\mathrm{B}'\mathrm{B}''$, we have $\phi_{\mathrm{A}} \ot \phi_{\mathrm{B}} \ket{\psi} = V_{\mathrm{A}} \ot V_{\mathrm{B}} \ket{\hat\psi}$. Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-unitary} therefore yields a state $\ket{\mathrm{aux}}$ on registers $\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'$ such that
   346		\[
   347			\bigl\| \phi_{\mathrm{A}} \ot \phi_{\mathrm{B}} \ket{\psi} - \ket{\mathrm{aux}} \ot \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M} \bigr\|^2 \leq \delta_{\mathrm{qld}}\;.
   348		\]
   349		% Transfer step added: the source (lines 1864--1875 of
   350		% 14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex) passes directly from the
   351		% conjugation estimates of lem:qld-unitary, which concern the
   352		% unitarily conjugated operators V (M_h ot Id) V^dagger, to the
   353		% corresponding estimates for the isometry phi, whose conjugation
   354		% inserts the projection onto its range; the range-projection
   355		% argument below supplies the missing step.
   356		Item~2 of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-unitary} concerns the unitarily conjugated operators $N^W_h = V_{\mathrm{A}} \, (M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h)_{\mathrm{A}} \, V_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger$, whereas conjugation by the isometry $\phi_{\mathrm{A}}$ additionally inserts the projection $Q_{\mathrm{A}} = \phi_{\mathrm{A}} \phi_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger = V_{\mathrm{A}} \, \bigl(\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}\bra{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}\bigr)_{\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''} \, V_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger$ onto the range of $\phi_{\mathrm{A}}$: since $(M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h)_{\mathrm{A}}$ and $\bigl(\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}\bra{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}\bigr)_{\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''}$ act on disjoint registers and hence commute,
   357		\[
   358			\phi_{\mathrm{A}} \, (M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h)_{\mathrm{A}} \, \phi_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger
   359			= V_{\mathrm{A}} \, \Bigl( (M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h)_{\mathrm{A}} \ot \bigl(\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}\bra{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}\bigr)_{\mathrm{A}'\mathrm{A}''} \Bigr) \, V_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger
   360			= N^W_h \, Q_{\mathrm{A}} = Q_{\mathrm{A}} \, N^W_h\;.
   361		\]
   362		The estimates transfer from $N^W_h$ to $\phi_{\mathrm{A}} \, (M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h)_{\mathrm{A}} \, \phi_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger$ as follows. Write $\ket{\Delta} = \ket{\mathrm{aux}} \ot \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}$ and $\ket{\vartheta} = \phi_{\mathrm{A}} \ot \phi_{\mathrm{B}} \ket{\psi}$. Since $\phi_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger \phi_{\mathrm{A}} = \Id$, the projection $\Id - Q_{\mathrm{A}}$ annihilates $\ket{\vartheta}$, so the displayed bound above gives
   363		\[
   364			\bigl\| (\Id - Q_{\mathrm{A}}) \ket{\Delta} \bigr\|^2
   365			= \bigl\| (\Id - Q_{\mathrm{A}}) (\ket{\Delta} - \ket{\vartheta}) \bigr\|^2
   366			\leq \bigl\| \ket{\Delta} - \ket{\vartheta} \bigr\|^2
   367			\leq \delta_{\mathrm{qld}}\;.
   368		\]
   369		Since the strategy is projective, the operators $N^W_h$, for $h \in \F_q^M$, are mutually orthogonal projectors summing to the identity, so $\sum_h \| N^W_h \ket{\xi} \|^2 = \| \ket{\xi} \|^2$ for every vector $\ket{\xi}$. Decomposing
   370		\[
   371			\bigl( \phi_{\mathrm{A}} \, (M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h)_{\mathrm{A}} \, \phi_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger - (\tau^W_h)_{\mathrm{A}''} \bigr) \ket{\Delta}
   372			= \bigl( N^W_h - (\tau^W_h)_{\mathrm{A}''} \bigr) \ket{\Delta} - N^W_h (\Id - Q_{\mathrm{A}}) \ket{\Delta}
   373		\]
   374		and summing the squared norms over $h$ via $\| \xi - \xi' \|^2 \leq 2\|\xi\|^2 + 2\|\xi'\|^2$, the first terms contribute $O(\delta_{\mathrm{qld}})$ by Item~2 of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-unitary} and the second terms contribute at most $2 \| (\Id - Q_{\mathrm{A}}) \ket{\Delta} \|^2 \leq 2\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}$; hence, for $W \in \{X,Z\}$,
   375		\[
   376			\phi_{\mathrm{A}} \, (M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h)_{\mathrm{A}} \, \phi_{\mathrm{A}}^\dagger \approx_{\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}} (\tau^W_h)_{\mathrm{A}''}
   377			\qquad \text{and, by the identical argument,} \qquad
   378			\phi_{\mathrm{B}} \, (M^{(\mathrm{Pauli},W)}_h)_{\mathrm{B}} \, \phi_{\mathrm{B}}^\dagger \approx_{\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}} (\tau^W_h)_{\mathrm{B}''}\;,
   379		\]
   380		where the $\approx$ statements hold with respect to the state $\ket{\mathrm{aux}} \ot \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}$ and the answer summation is over $h \in \F_q^M$; the constant implicit in $\approx_{\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}}$ (Definition~\ref{def:povm-distance}) absorbs the factors accumulated above. This shows that the game $\mathfrak{G}^{\mathrm{Pauli}}_{(q,m,d)}$ is a self-test, with robustness $\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}(\eps,m,d,q)$, for the canonical Pauli strategy of Lemma~\ref{lem:pauli-completeness}. Identifying the registers $\mathrm{A}\mathrm{A}'$ with $\mathrm{A}'$ and $\mathrm{B}\mathrm{B}'$ with $\mathrm{B}'$ matches the statement of Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli}, in which $\phi_{\mathrm{A}}\colon \mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{A}} \to \mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{A}'} \ot \mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{A}''}$. Finally, unpacking the dependence on the parameters $\eps, m, d, q$, the function $\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}(\eps,m,d,q) = O(\delta_P^{1/4} + md/q)$ has the form $a(md)^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$ for universal constants $a > 1$ and $0 < b < 1$; here $\delta_P = C(\delta_G + \sqrt{\eps} + md/q)$ and $\delta_G$ already has that form. See Remark~\ref{rem:pauli-robustness-form} for the reconciliation with the statement of Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli}.
   381	\end{proof}
   382	
   383	\begin{remark}[Norm conventions in the robustness bound]\label{rem:pauli-robustness-form}
   384		The proof above, following the source, establishes the first conclusion of Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli} in the squared form $\| \phi_{\mathrm{A}} \ot \phi_{\mathrm{B}} \ket{\psi} - \ket{\mathrm{aux}} \ot \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M} \|^2 \leq \delta_{\mathrm{qld}}$, whereas the theorem bounds the unsquared norm by $\delta_{\mathrm{qld}}(\eps,m,d,q)$. The two are reconciled by replacing the exponent $b$ with $b/2$ and enlarging $a$, since the class of functions $a(md)^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$ is closed under square roots up to such adjustments of the universal constants. Similarly, the closing sentence of the source proof asserts constants $a > 1$ and $0 < b < 1$, while Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli} requires only $a \geq 1$ and $0 < b < 1$; the former implies the latter.
   385	\end{remark}

   102	  self_consistent : ∀ p1 p2 : Placement, p1.IsOpposite p2 ->
   103	    opFamilyDistSq
   104	      (uniformDistribution
   105	        ((Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P) × (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P)))
   106	      (fun xz ab => S.place p1 ((Q p1.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))
   107	      (fun xz ab => S.place p2 ((Q p2.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))
   108	      S.psiHat <= δ
   109	  /-- Joint point measurements are close to the ordered `X`-then-`Z` product. -/
   110	  consistent_XZ : ∀ p1 p2 : Placement, p1.IsOpposite p2 ->
   111	    opFamilyDistSq
   112	      (uniformDistribution
   113	        ((Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P) × (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P)))
   114	      (fun xz ab => S.place p1 ((Q p1.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))
   115	      (fun xz ab => S.place p2
   116	        ((S.pointMeasExp p2.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1 *
   117	          (S.pointMeasExp p2.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2))
   118	      S.psiHat <= δ
   119	  /-- Joint point measurements are close to the ordered `Z`-then-`X` product. -/
   120	  consistent_ZX : ∀ p1 p2 : Placement, p1.IsOpposite p2 ->

   123	        ((Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P) × (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P)))
   124	      (fun xz ab => S.place p1 ((Q p1.side xz.1 xz.2).effect ab))

   126	        ((S.pointMeasExp p2.side .Z xz.2).effect ab.2 *
   127	          (S.pointMeasExp p2.side .X xz.1).effect ab.1))

   130	/-- Joint line measurements and their evaluation consistency from
   131	`lem:qld-xz-lines`, paper lines 882--894.  Evaluation uses explicit `Option`
   132	outcomes, including the class of answers not determined at the sampled point. -/
   133	structure CombinedLinesWitness {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε δQ : ℝ}
   134	    (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (points : CombinedPointsWitness S δQ)
   135	    (δ : ℝ) where
   136	  /-- The complete paired-line measurement on each expanded local space. -/
   137	  T : (side : PlayerSide) ->
   138	    LineDesc P.toLdParams -> LineDesc P.toLdParams ->
   139	    Measurement
   140	      (DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d) ×
   141	        DegPoly P.toLdParams (P.m * P.d))
   142	      (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side)
   143	  /-- On an axis-parallel X line, outcomes outside degree `d` have zero effect. -/
   144	  axis_degree_X : ∀ side lineX lineZ fX fZ,
   145	    lineX.kind = .axis -> Not (DegPoly.FitsDegree P.d fX) ->
   146	      (T side lineX lineZ).effect (fX, fZ) = 0
   147	  /-- On an axis-parallel Z line, outcomes outside degree `d` have zero effect. -/
   148	  axis_degree_Z : ∀ side lineX lineZ fX fZ,
   149	    lineZ.kind = .axis -> Not (DegPoly.FitsDegree P.d fZ) ->
   150	      (T side lineX lineZ).effect (fX, fZ) = 0
   151	  /-- Evaluated line pairs are consistent with the completed point-pair
   152	  measurement on every directed opposite placement. -/
   153	  consistent : ∀ p1 p2 : Placement, p1.IsOpposite p2 ->
   154	    consistencyDefect
   155	      (Distribution.prod (linePointDist P.toLdParams)
   156	        (linePointDist P.toLdParams))
   157	      (fun sample answer => S.place p1
   158	        (((T p1.side sample.1.1 sample.2.1).postprocess fun fs =>
   159	          (evalOpt sample.1.1 sample.1.2 fs.1,
   160	            evalOpt sample.2.1 sample.2.2 fs.2)).effect answer))
   161	      (fun sample answer => S.place p2
   162	        (((points.Q p2.side sample.1.2 sample.2.2).postprocess fun ab =>
   163	          (some ab.1, some ab.2)).effect answer))
   164	      S.psiHat <= δ

   166	/-! ## The subline distribution -/
   167	
   168	/-- A tuple consisting of an extended line and its projected X and Z lines. -/
   169	abbrev SubLineTriple (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
   170	  DirectLineDesc P.extendedDirectLd ×
   171	    (LineDesc P.toLdParams × LineDesc P.toLdParams)
   172	
   173	/-- An extended line tuple together with a point sampled uniformly on it. -/
   174	abbrev SubLinePointSample (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
   175	  SubLineTriple P ×
   176	    (Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m -> DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)
   177	
   178	/-- The shared restricted line kind and two coordinate indices in one mixture
   179	component of the subline law. -/
   180	abbrev SubLineComponent (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
   181	  LineKind × (Fin P.m × Fin P.m)
   182	
   183	/-- Select the restricted line-point distribution of a given kind and index. -/
   184	noncomputable def restrictedLinePointDist (P : AdmissibleParams)
   185	    (kind : LineKind) (i : Fin P.m) :
   186	    Distribution (LineDesc P.toLdParams × (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P)) :=
   187	  match kind with
   188	  | .axis => restrictedALineDist P.toLdParams i
   189	  | .diagonal => restrictedDLineDist P.toLdParams i
   190	
   191	/-- Sample a subline tuple and then a uniform affine parameter on its
   192	extended line. -/
   193	noncomputable def subLinePointDist (P : AdmissibleParams)
   194	    (D : Distribution (SubLineTriple P)) :
   195	    Distribution (SubLinePointSample P) :=
   196	  (Distribution.prod D
   197	    (uniformDistribution (DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd))).map fun sample =>
   198	      (sample.1, sample.1.1.base + sample.2 • sample.1.1.direction)
   199	
   200	/-- Retain the projected line pair and the X projection of an extended point. -/
   201	def subLineXProjection {P : AdmissibleParams} (sample : SubLinePointSample P) :
   202	    (LineDesc P.toLdParams × LineDesc P.toLdParams) ×
   203	      (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P) :=
   204	  (sample.1.2, projX (directPointToPauli P sample.2))
   205	
   206	/-- Retain the projected line pair and the Z projection of an extended point. -/
   207	def subLineZProjection {P : AdmissibleParams} (sample : SubLinePointSample P) :
   208	    (LineDesc P.toLdParams × LineDesc P.toLdParams) ×
   209	      (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P) :=
   210	  (sample.1.2, projZ (directPointToPauli P sample.2))
   211	
   212	/-- The X-point marginal associated with one restricted product component. -/
   213	noncomputable def subLineXComponentDist (P : AdmissibleParams)
   214	    (component : SubLineComponent P) :
   215	    Distribution
   216	      ((LineDesc P.toLdParams × LineDesc P.toLdParams) ×
   217	        (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P)) :=
   218	  (Distribution.prod
   219	    (restrictedLinePointDist P component.1 component.2.1)
   220	    ((restrictedLinePointDist P component.1 component.2.2).map Prod.fst)).map
   221	      fun sample => ((sample.1.1, sample.2), sample.1.2)
   222	
   223	/-- The Z-point marginal associated with one restricted product component. -/
   224	noncomputable def subLineZComponentDist (P : AdmissibleParams)
   225	    (component : SubLineComponent P) :
   226	    Distribution
   227	      ((LineDesc P.toLdParams × LineDesc P.toLdParams) ×
   228	        (Fin P.m -> PauliScalar P)) :=
   229	  (Distribution.prod
   230	    ((restrictedLinePointDist P component.1 component.2.1).map Prod.fst)
   231	    (restrictedLinePointDist P component.1 component.2.2)).map
   232	      fun sample => ((sample.1, sample.2.1), sample.2.2)
   233	
   234	/-- The subline distribution of `lem:qld-sublines`, paper lines 1063--1069.
   235	Its source-mixture field records the X and Z point marginals separately; it
   236	does not assert a joint conditional law for the pair of projected points. -/
   237	structure SubLineWitness (P : AdmissibleParams) where
   238	  /-- The actual distribution of an extended line and two projected lines. -/
   239	  D : Distribution (SubLineTriple P)
   240	  /-- The distribution has total mass one. -/
   241	  isProbability : D.IsProbability
   242	  /-- Its extended-line marginal is the direct line-point marginal. -/
   243	  extended_marginal : D.map Prod.fst =
   244	    (directLinePointDist P.extendedDirectLd).map Prod.fst
   245	  /-- Every point of an extended line projects onto both stored source lines. -/
   246	  incidence : ∀ sample ∈ D.support, ∀ u ∈ sample.1.pointSet,
   247	    projX (directPointToPauli P u) ∈ sample.2.1.pointSet ∧
   248	      projZ (directPointToPauli P u) ∈ sample.2.2.pointSet
   249	  /-- Each line triple carries affine data sufficient for
   250	  `combineLinePoly_spec`. -/
   251	  compatibility : ∀ sample ∈ D.support,
   252	    ∃ aX bX aZ bZ uAlpha vAlpha uBeta vBeta : PauliScalar P,
   253	      IsCombineLineCompatible
   254	        (directPointToPauli P sample.1.base)
   255	        (directPointToPauli P sample.1.direction)
   256	        sample.2.1.base sample.2.1.direction
   257	        sample.2.2.base sample.2.2.direction
   258	        aX bX aZ bZ uAlpha vAlpha uBeta vBeta
   259	  /-- Each one-point projected marginal is a mixture of restricted product
   260	  laws.  No equality for their joint conditional law is claimed. -/

     4	/-!
     5	# Polynomial combination and restricted line distributions
     6	
     7	This file contains the concrete definitions at the foundation of the
     8	Chapter 15 combining argument.  A pair of bounded individual-degree
     9	polynomials is embedded into the two coordinate blocks of an extended
    10	polynomial.  On lines, explicit affine reparameterizations are composed with
    11	coefficient-list polynomials.  The original-dimensional restricted line laws
    12	are formed before decoding, while their field seed is still present.
    13	
    14	## References
    15	
    16	The combining map is `def:combine-map` in
    17	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:445-480`, with paper origin
    18	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`.
    19	The restricted laws are `def:ith-restricted-line` in blueprint lines 578--592,
    20	with paper origin in the same source at lines 1038--1048.
    21	-/
    22	
    23	open scoped BigOperators
    24	
    25	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    26	
    27	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    28	open MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries

    31	
    32	/-- The bounded individual-degree polynomial outcome used by the global
    33	pair measurement.  This is the actual `polyFunc` subtype from
    34	`def:polyfunc`, not a coefficient-box replacement. -/
    35	noncomputable abbrev Poly (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
    36	  ↥(MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.polyFunc P.m (PauliScalar P) P.d)
    37	
    38	/-- Pairs of bounded polynomial representatives returned by the global
    39	measurement in `lem:qld-4-7`. -/
    40	noncomputable abbrev PolyPair (P : AdmissibleParams) := Poly P × Poly P
    41	
    42	/-- Split the extended coordinate set into the `X` block, the `Z` block, and
    43	the two scalar coordinates.  This is formalization-only coordinate plumbing
    44	for `def:combine-map`, blueprint
    45	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:445-480`, paper
    46	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
    47	def finCombineEquiv (m : ℕ) :
    48	    Fin (2 * m + 2) ≃ ((Fin m ⊕ Fin m) ⊕ Fin 2) :=
    49	  (finCongr (by omega)).trans
    50	    (finSumFinEquiv.symm.trans
    51	      (Equiv.sumCongr finSumFinEquiv.symm (Equiv.refl (Fin 2))))
    52	
    53	/-- Embed an `X`-block coordinate into the extended coordinate set. -/
    54	def embX (m : ℕ) : Fin m → Fin (2 * m + 2) :=
    55	  fun i => (finCombineEquiv m).symm (.inl (.inl i))
    56	
    57	/-- Embed a `Z`-block coordinate into the extended coordinate set. -/
    58	def embZ (m : ℕ) : Fin m → Fin (2 * m + 2) :=
    59	  fun i => (finCombineEquiv m).symm (.inl (.inr i))
    60	
    61	/-- The extended coordinate occupied by the scalar `alpha`. -/
    62	def alphaVar (m : ℕ) : Fin (2 * m + 2) :=
    63	  (finCombineEquiv m).symm (.inr 0)
    64	
    65	/-- The extended coordinate occupied by the scalar `beta`. -/
    66	def betaVar (m : ℕ) : Fin (2 * m + 2) :=
    67	  (finCombineEquiv m).symm (.inr 1)
    68	
    69	/-- Project an extended point onto its `X` coordinate block. -/
    70	def projX {K : Type*} {m : ℕ} (u : Fin (2 * m + 2) → K) : Fin m → K :=
    71	  fun i => u (embX m i)
    72	
    73	/-- Project an extended point onto its `Z` coordinate block. -/
    74	def projZ {K : Type*} {m : ℕ} (u : Fin (2 * m + 2) → K) : Fin m → K :=
    75	  fun i => u (embZ m i)
    76	
    77	/-- Combine two multivariate polynomials by the formula
    78	`alpha * f(x) + beta * g(z)` from `def:combine-map`.
    79	
    80	Blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:445-480`; paper
    81	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-983`. -/
    82	noncomputable def combinePoly {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K] {m : ℕ}
    83	    (f g : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K) : MvPolynomial (Fin (2 * m + 2)) K :=
    84	  MvPolynomial.X (alphaVar m) * MvPolynomial.rename (embX m) f +
    85	    MvPolynomial.X (betaVar m) * MvPolynomial.rename (embZ m) g
    86	
    87	/-- Evaluation of `combinePoly` is the displayed combining formula. -/
    88	theorem combinePoly_eval {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K] {m : ℕ}
    89	    (f g : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K) (u : Fin (2 * m + 2) → K) :
    90	    MvPolynomial.eval u (combinePoly f g) =
    91	      u (alphaVar m) * MvPolynomial.eval (projX u) f +
    92	        u (betaVar m) * MvPolynomial.eval (projZ u) g := by
    93	  change MvPolynomial.eval u (combinePoly f g) =
    94	    u (alphaVar m) * MvPolynomial.eval (u ∘ embX m) f +
    95	      u (betaVar m) * MvPolynomial.eval (u ∘ embZ m) g
    96	  simp [combinePoly, MvPolynomial.eval_rename]

    98	/-- The combining polynomial has individual degree at most `d` when
    99	`hd : 1 ≤ d`.  The coordinate blocks are disjoint: `f` depends only on the
   100	`x` variables and `g` only on the `z` variables, so multiplication by `alpha`
   101	or `beta` preserves the degree bound on those old coordinates and gives degree
   102	one only in the corresponding fresh coordinate.  Thus `hd` supplies exactly
   103	the needed bound on the two fresh coordinates; no `d + 1` bound is introduced.
   104	The statement is the well-definedness assertion in
   105	`def:combine-map`, blueprint
   106	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:445-480`, with source context
   107	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-983` and the
   108	boundary-hypothesis discussion in `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`.
   109	-/
   110	theorem combinePoly_mem_polyFunc {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K] {m d : ℕ}
   111	    (hd : 1 ≤ d) {f g : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K}
   112	    (hf : f ∈ polyFunc m K d) (hg : g ∈ polyFunc m K d) :
   113	    combinePoly f g ∈ polyFunc (2 * m + 2) K d := by
   114	  sorry
   115	
   116	/-- Evaluate one member of a global polynomial pair at a point, selecting the
   117	component by Pauli basis.  This is formalization-only support for
   118	`lem:qld-4-7`, paper
   119	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1267-1274`. -/
   120	def evalAt {P : AdmissibleParams} (W : PauliKind)
   121	    (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (pair : PolyPair P) : PauliScalar P :=
   122	  match W with
   123	  | .X => MvPolynomial.eval u pair.1.1
   124	  | .Z => MvPolynomial.eval u pair.2.1
   125	
   126	/-- Interpret a bounded coefficient list as an ordinary univariate
   127	polynomial.  This helper makes the line-combination definition use Mathlib's
   128	actual polynomial composition operation. -/
   129	noncomputable def linePolynomialOfCoefficients {K : Type*} [Semiring K]
   130	    {c : ℕ} (f : Fin (c + 1) → K) : Polynomial K :=
   131	  ∑ i : Fin (c + 1), Polynomial.C (f i) * Polynomial.X ^ i.val
   132	
   133	/-- Evaluating the polynomial represented by a coefficient list agrees with
   134	`evalCoefficient`. -/
   135	theorem linePolynomialOfCoefficients_eval {K : Type*} [Semiring K]
   136	    {c : ℕ} (f : Fin (c + 1) → K) (t : K) :
   137	    (linePolynomialOfCoefficients f).eval t = evalCoefficient f t := by
   138	  change Polynomial.eval t
   139	      (∑ i ∈ Finset.univ, Polynomial.C (f i) * Polynomial.X ^ i.val) =
   140	    ∑ i ∈ Finset.univ, f i * t ^ i.val
   141	  rw [Polynomial.eval_finsetSum]
   142	  simp
   143	
   144	/-- The univariate polynomial before coefficient extraction in
   145	`combineLinePoly`.  The four first scalars describe the affine parameters on
   146	the two projected lines; the last four are the affine `alpha` and `beta`
   147	coordinates of the extended line. -/
   148	noncomputable def combineLinePolynomial {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K] {c : ℕ}
   149	    (aX bX aZ bZ uα vα uβ vβ : K)
   150	    (f g : Fin (c + 1) → K) : Polynomial K :=
   151	  (Polynomial.C uα + Polynomial.C vα * Polynomial.X) *
   152	      (linePolynomialOfCoefficients f).comp
   153	        (Polynomial.C aX + Polynomial.C bX * Polynomial.X) +
   154	    (Polynomial.C uβ + Polynomial.C vβ * Polynomial.X) *
   155	      (linePolynomialOfCoefficients g).comp
   156	        (Polynomial.C aZ + Polynomial.C bZ * Polynomial.X)
   157	
   158	/-- The polynomial underlying `combineLinePoly` has degree at most `c + 1`.
   159	This is the degree assertion accompanying Equation `eq:combine-lines` in
   160	`def:combine-map`, blueprint
   161	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:459-479`, paper
   162	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:984-989`. -/
   163	theorem combineLinePolynomial_natDegree_le {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K] {c : ℕ}
   164	    (aX bX aZ bZ uα vα uβ vβ : K) (f g : Fin (c + 1) → K) :
   165	    (combineLinePolynomial aX bX aZ bZ uα vα uβ vβ f g).natDegree ≤ c + 1 := by
   166	  sorry

   168	/-- Combine two degree-`c` line polynomials using explicit affine
   169	reparameterizations.  Coefficients through degree `c + 1` are extracted from
   170	the genuine composed polynomial, so the definition has no incompatibility
   171	fallback.
   172	
   173	This is Equation `eq:combine-lines` in `def:combine-map`, blueprint
   174	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:459-479`, paper
   175	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:984-989`. -/
   176	noncomputable def combineLinePoly {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K] {c : ℕ}
   177	    (aX bX aZ bZ uα vα uβ vβ : K)
   178	    (f g : Fin (c + 1) → K) : Fin (c + 1 + 1) → K :=
   179	  fun i => (combineLinePolynomial aX bX aZ bZ uα vα uβ vβ f g).coeff i.val
   180	
   181	/-- Compatibility of an extended line with two projected lines and their
   182	explicit affine parameters.  This is precisely the domain condition preceding
   183	Equation `eq:combine-lines`; it is data supplied by the future subline
   184	construction, not a fallback branch in `combineLinePoly`. -/
   185	def IsCombineLineCompatible {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
   186	    (u v : Fin (2 * m + 2) → K)
   187	    (uX vX uZ vZ : Fin m → K)
   188	    (aX bX aZ bZ uα vα uβ vβ : K) : Prop :=
   189	  u (alphaVar m) = uα ∧ v (alphaVar m) = vα ∧
   190	    u (betaVar m) = uβ ∧ v (betaVar m) = vβ ∧
   191	    ∀ t : K,
   192	      projX (u + t • v) = uX + (aX + bX * t) • vX ∧
   193	        projZ (u + t • v) = uZ + (aZ + bZ * t) • vZ
   194	
   195	/-- Under explicit line compatibility, `combineLinePoly` satisfies the
   196	advertised line equation and the two projected points have the stated affine
   197	parameters.  This is the specification obligation for Equation
   198	`eq:combine-lines`, blueprint
   199	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:459-479`, paper
   200	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:984-989`. -/
   201	theorem combineLinePoly_spec {K : Type*} [Field K] {m c : ℕ}
   202	    (u v : Fin (2 * m + 2) → K) (uX vX uZ vZ : Fin m → K)
   203	    (aX bX aZ bZ uα vα uβ vβ : K) (f g : Fin (c + 1) → K)
   204	    (hcompat : IsCombineLineCompatible u v uX vX uZ vZ
   205	      aX bX aZ bZ uα vα uβ vβ) :
   206	    ∀ t : K,
   207	      projX (u + t • v) = uX + (aX + bX * t) • vX ∧
   208	      projZ (u + t • v) = uZ + (aZ + bZ * t) • vZ ∧
   209	      evalCoefficient
   210	          (combineLinePoly aX bX aZ bZ uα vα uβ vβ f g) t =
   211	        (uα + t * vα) * evalCoefficient f (aX + bX * t) +
   212	          (uβ + t * vβ) * evalCoefficient g (aZ + bZ * t) := by
   213	  sorry

   219	    (sample : LdSpace L × LdSpace L) : Prop :=

   223	instance restrictedLineSeedEvent_decidablePred (L : LdParams) (i : Fin L.m) :

   234	theorem restrictedALineSeedEvent_positive (L : LdParams) (i : Fin L.m) :

     4	# The low-degree encoding
     5	
     6	This module encodes the Boolean subcube by multilinear indicator polynomials
     7	and packages the resulting low-degree code as honest polynomial representatives.
     8	
     9	## References
    10	
    11	The source-facing nodes are `def:polynomials-degree`,
    12	`def:low-degree-encoding`, and `def:indicator-vector` in
    13	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:321-417`; the paper origin is
    14	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    15	The polynomial class `def:polyfunc` is reused from
    16	`MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.polyFunc` (the LDT formalization).
    17	-/
    18	
    19	open scoped BigOperators
    20	open MvPolynomial
    21	
    22	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    23	
    24	/- The Boolean cube indexes the `2^m` qudits in the low-degree encoding. -/
    25	/-- The Boolean cube indexing the `2^m` qudits of the test.  This is the index
    26	type in `def:low-degree-encoding`, blueprint
    27	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:381-401`, paper origin
    28	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    29	-/
    30	abbrev Cube (m : ℕ) := Fin m → Bool
    31	
    32	/--
    33	The representative polynomial which is `1` at `y` on the Boolean cube and
    34	zero at the other cube points.  This is the indicator polynomial in
    35	`def:low-degree-encoding` (blueprint lines 381-401; paper
    36	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`).
    37	-/
    38	noncomputable def indicatorPoly {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ} (y : Cube m) :
    39	    MvPolynomial (Fin m) K :=
    40	  ∏ i : Fin m, if y i then X i else (1 - X i)
    41	
    42	/--
    43	The multilinear low-degree encoding of a coefficient string.  Polynomial
    44	representatives are used, as fixed by issue #0004, rather than quotienting by
    45	functional equality.  Blueprint: `def:low-degree-encoding`,
    46	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:381-401`; paper origin:
    47	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    48	-/
    49	noncomputable def lowDegreeEncoding {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ}
    50	    (a : Cube m → K) : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K :=
    51	  ∑ y : Cube m, a y • indicatorPoly y

    55	/-- Evaluation shorthand for the low-degree encoding.  Blueprint

    58	-/
    59	noncomputable def lowDegreeEnc {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ}
    60	    (a : Cube m → K) (x : Fin m → K) : K :=

    62	
    63	/--

    19	`def:decoding-map`; blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper
    20	`04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`. -/
    21	def boolToScalar {K : Type*} [Field K] : Bool → K
    22	  | false => 0
    23	  | true => 1
    24	
    25	/-- The coordinatewise Boolean-cube embedding used by
    26	`def:decoding-map`; blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper
    27	`04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`. -/
    28	def cubeEmbed {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ} : Cube m → (Fin m → K) :=
    29	  fun y i => boolToScalar (y i)
    30	
    31	/-- The decoding map `def:decoding-map`, blueprint
    32	`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper `04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`. -/
    33	noncomputable def decodeAt {K : Type*} [Field K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ}
    34	    (H : Finset K) (g : (Fin m → K) → K) : Cube m → K :=
    35	  fun y => if g (cubeEmbed y) ∈ H then g (cubeEmbed y) else 0
    36	
    37	/-- Boolean specialization of `def:decoding-map`, blueprint
    38	`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper `04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`. -/
    39	noncomputable abbrev decodeBool {K : Type*} [Field K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ}
    40	    (g : (Fin m → K) → K) : Cube m → K :=
    41	  decodeAt ({0, 1} : Finset K) g

    43	/-- The full-field specialization of `decodeAt` used by the generic algebra
    44	layer.  The Chapter 16 `Poly`-facing name is defined in `Algebra/Decoding.lean`.
    45	Every value is retained because the filter is `H = Finset.univ`, so this is the
    46	cube-indexed evaluation of a polynomial representative.  The restricted
    47	decoder identity remains separate and is only available for encoding
    48	representatives; no unrestricted interpolation identity is asserted here.
    49	
    50	This is the `H = \F_q` reading of `def:decoding-map`, blueprint
    51	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, used by Chapter 16 at
    52	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:11-20`; paper origin
    53	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1419-1420` and
    54	the correction recorded in `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_decoding-identity.tex`. -/
    55	noncomputable def decodeFqRep {K : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ}
    56	    (g : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K) : Cube m → K :=
    57	  decodeAt (Finset.univ : Finset K) (fun x => MvPolynomial.eval x g)
    58	
    59	/-- A polynomial representative lies in the low-degree encoding image when it
    60	is exactly the multilinear representative reconstructed from its full-field
    61	decoder.  This predicate is used to state the support restriction required by

    63	functions with their representatives.

    65	See `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_decoding-identity.tex:87-116`. -/
    66	def IsEncodingRep {K : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ}

   154	  warning; the dependency edge should explain where the auxiliary result is
   155	  used.

   158	  is acceptable only when the Lean statement is intentionally recorded but the
   159	  proof remains tracked as incomplete.
